# unicode_bidi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicode-bidi/

## Expand description

This crate implements the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/) for display of mixed
right-to-left and left-to-right text.  It is written in safe Rust, compatible with the
current stable release.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use unicode_bidi::BidiInfo;
// This example text is defined using `concat!` because some browsers
// and text editors have trouble displaying bidi strings.
let text = concat![
  "א",
  "ב",
  "ג",
  "a",
  "b",
  "c",
];
// Resolve embedding levels within the text.  Pass `None` to detect the
// paragraph level automatically.
let bidi_info = BidiInfo::new(&text, None);
// This paragraph has embedding level 1 because its first strong character is RTL.
assert_eq!(bidi_info.paragraphs.len(), 1);
let para = &bidi_info.paragraphs[0];
assert_eq!(para.level.number(), 1);
assert_eq!(para.level.is_rtl(), true);
// Re-ordering is done after wrapping each paragraph into a sequence of
// lines. For this example, I'll just use a single line that spans the
// entire paragraph.
let line = para.range.clone();
let display = bidi_info.reorder_line(para, line);
assert_eq!(display, concat![
  "a",
  "b",
  "c",
  "ג",
  "ב",
  "א",
]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `std`: Enabled by default, but can be disabled to make- `unicode_bidi`- `#![no_std]`+- `alloc`compatible.
- `hardcoded-data`: Enabled by default. Includes hardcoded Unicode bidi data and more convenient APIs.
- `serde`: Adds [- `serde::Serialize`] and [- `serde::Deserialize`] implementations to relevant types.

- `pub use crate::level::`- [RTL_LEVEL](https://docs.rs/level/constant.RTL_LEVEL.html);

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Text](https://docs.rs/trait.TextSource.html)- Source
- Trait that abstracts over a text source for use by the bidi algorithms.
We implement this for str (UTF-8) and for [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)(UTF-16, native-endian). (For internal unicode-bidi use; API may be unstable.) This trait is sealed and cannot be implemented for types outside this crate.

- Get the base direction of the text provided according to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_base_direction_full.html)- base_ - direction_ - full
- Get the base direction of the text provided according to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm, considering the full text if the first paragraph is all-neutral.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_base_direction_full_with_data_source.html)- base_ - direction_ - full_ - with_ - data_ - source
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_base_direction_with_data_source.html)- base_ - direction_ - with_ - data_ - source

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# gdscript_ide - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/gdscript_ide/

## Expand description

`gdscript-ide` — the public, engine-/protocol-neutral analysis API.

Modeled on rust-analyzer’s `ide::AnalysisHost` / `ide::Analysis`
(`plans/01-ARCHITECTURE.md` §2). [ AnalysisHost](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html) is the single mutable owner of the
input world;

[is a cheap, cloneable,](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Send` snapshot whose queries take
byte offsets and return plain `serde` result structs from `gdscript-base` — never
`lsp-types`. Each client (LSP server, the guitkx adapter, the CLI, the WASM
playground) maps these POD results to its own protocol.Phase 3 (M0) swaps the engine behind these types from a plain VFS map to a **salsa**
query graph in [ gdscript_db](https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_db/index.html): the input world is now

`FileText` salsa inputs, mutated
through `apply_change`; [is a cloned database handle (salsa handles are](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Clone + Send`, replacing the old `Arc<map>` snapshot). Cancellation is now *real*— a concurrent

`apply_change` cancels in-flight reads on outstanding handles, which unwind
into `Err(Cancelled)` at the query boundary (see [`catch`]). The public API shape is
unchanged. The crate stays `wasm32`-safe (CI guards this).This is the analyzer’s **public Rust API**, so every public item is documented and
`#![deny(missing_docs)]` keeps it that way.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)
- An immutable snapshot of the world — a cloned salsa handle. Every query is `Cancellable``apply_change`cancels in-flight reads, which the client re-issues against the fresh snapshot.
- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html)- Host
- The single mutable owner of analysis state — one per project/workspace.
- [Change](https://docs.rs/struct.Change.html)
- A batch of input changes. `None`text removes the file.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Warning](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html)- Override
- Re-exported so clients can set the warning-strictness override without depending on
`gdscript-db`directly. See`AnalysisHost::set_warning_override``gdscript-hir`/`gdscript-ide`depend on.`#[salsa::db]`on the*trait*makes it a salsa supertrait, so any`&dyn Db`upcasts to`&dyn salsa::Database`and every`#[salsa::tracked]`free function downstream can take`db: &dyn Db`. A host/CLI-level override of the warning-strictness baseline`type_diagnostics`resolves against (regardless of`project.godot`presence). A plain (non-salsa) per-session policy knob: it is read**only**inside the non-tracked`type_diagnostics`, so it never enters the salsa query graph and cannot break the W1 firewall (a warning-level change must never re-run inference).

# gdscript_hir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/

## Expand description

`gdscript-hir` — the semantic / type layer.

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Lowers the AST to a HIR (an `ItemTree` of signatures + per-function `Body`), runs name resolution
(local → class member → inherited → global), gradual type inference (Variant by default,
`:=`/annotations, member lookup over the engine inheritance table, `is`/`as` narrowing), and the
GDScript warning checks. Single-file in Phase 2; project-wide + scene-aware later.

Phase 2 builds this out bottom-up: the type model ([ ty](https://docs.rs/ty/index.html)), then the item tree, body, name
resolution, and inference. Must build for

`wasm32`.## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [body](https://docs.rs/body/index.html)
- Body lowering (Playbook §3.1/§3.4): a function body (or a class-level initializer
expression) lowered from the CST into a flat arena of `Expr``Stmt``ExprId``StmtId``BodySourceMap``ExprId``ExprId`through this source map, then reads the inferred type from`crate::infer`
- [def](https://docs.rs/def/index.html)
- Canonical symbol identity + cursor classification (Playbook §3.M5) — the basis of cross-file navigation (find-references, rename, goto-definition).
- [flow](https://docs.rs/flow/index.html)
- Per-body control-flow narrowing (Phase-6 Workstream 2).
- [infer](https://docs.rs/infer/index.html)
- Gradual type inference (Playbook §3.3–§3.6 + §5): a single forward, bottom-up,
bidirectional walk over a lowered `Body`*structure*, Pyright’s gradual*semantics*).
- [item_](https://docs.rs/item_tree/index.html)- tree
- The item tree (Playbook §3.1): a signature-level view of one `.gd`file — its`class_name`,`extends`target, and class members (funcs/vars/consts/signals/enums/inner classes) — lowered from the CST**without reading any function body**.
- [project](https://docs.rs/project/index.html)
- `project.godot`autoload parsing (Playbook §3.M4).
- [queries](https://docs.rs/queries/index.html)
- The salsa-tracked entry points for the semantic layer, layered on `gdscript-db`’s`parse`
- [resolve](https://docs.rs/resolve/index.html)
- Name & type resolution (Playbook §3.2/§3.5): the `resolve_external``Ty``ClassScope`
- [ty](https://docs.rs/ty/index.html)
- The Phase-2 type model (Playbook §2/§3.5): the gradual `Ty``Variant`, the hard/soft`TypeSource``is_assignable`compatibility check, and`TyRef`→`Ty`resolution against the engine API.
- [warnings](https://docs.rs/warnings/index.html)
- The Godot warning catalog + the emit-then-gate seam (Phase-6 Workstream 1).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AstPtr](https://docs.rs/struct.AstPtr.html)
- A reparse-stable pointer to a syntax node — its `SyntaxKind``TextRange``SyntaxNodePtr`). Because it is plain`Copy`data keyed on text position, identical source re-parses to the identical pointer, which is what lets the`crate::item_tree::ItemTree``Eq`while still being able to recover the CST node for deferred body lowering / initializer inference.

# hpw_convert_eip681 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hpw-convert-eip681/0.1.0/hpw_convert_eip681/

## Expand description

HashPort Walletが発行するJPYC決済リンクをパースし、EIP-681（ERC-681） 決済URI、あるいはその構成要素（アドレス、金額）に変換する、非公式・ HashPortとは無関係のライブラリ。

純粋なクライアントサイドの文字列/URLパースのみを行い、HashPortの サーバーへは一切ネットワークリクエストを送らない。HashPort Walletを 持たない人が、提示されたQR/リンクを読み取り別のウォレットで支払うための 相互運用ツールとして存在する。HashPortの承認・提携を受けたものではない。

現時点ではPolygon（chainId 137）とJPYCのみに対応する。

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html)
- An Ethereum address, 20 bytes in length.
- [Address](https://docs.rs/struct.AddressAmount.html)- Amount
- [ChainId](https://docs.rs/struct.ChainId.html)
- [Parsed](https://docs.rs/struct.ParsedLink.html)- Link

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_supported.html)- supported
- `url`がこのクレートでパース可能なHashPort Wallet決済リンクかどうかを 返す。- `parse`- `parse`を直接呼び出すこと。
- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- HashPort Wallet決済リンクをパースし、構成要素に分解する。
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_checksum.html)- checksum
- オプションの厳密なEIP-55チェックサム検証。`raw`はアドレスの チェックサム表記と一字一句完全に一致する必要がある。大文字のみ・ 小文字のみの表記は、同じアドレスを指していてもチェックサム情報を 持たないため拒否される。

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [U256](https://docs.rs/type.U256.html)
- 256-bit [unsigned integer type](https://docs.rs/ruint/1.18.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ruint/struct.Uint.html), consisting of 4, 64-bit limbs.

# cairn-lang-cli 2026.7.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cairn-lang-cli/2026.7.2

# cairn-lang-cli

The `cairn` command-line interface. This is the only Cairn crate that ships an executable; it wires
the [ cairn-lang-core](https://docs.rs/cairn-lang-core/README.md) compiler, the format backends in

[, and (when described logically) the redstone synthesizer in](https://docs.rs/cairn-lang-formats/README.md)

`cairn-lang-formats`[into the subcommands an author actually types.](https://docs.rs/cairn-lang-redstone/README.md)

`cairn-lang-redstone`## Status

Skeleton. The current binary recognizes `--version` / `--help` and prints a stub usage block; every
real subcommand returns a "not implemented yet" error.

## Subcommands (planned)

The CLI surface follows the spec; each subcommand maps onto a chapter so the help text and the normative document can never drift.

| Subcommand | Purpose | Spec reference |
|---|---|---|
| `cairn compile <file.crn> --edition <e> --target <v>` | Compile a `.crn`source to NBT / schematic output for`(edition, version)` | [compilation §4.2](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/compilation/),[versioning-editions](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/versioning-editions/) |
| `cairn import <schematic> --mode raw|l1` | Faithful transliteration of `.nbt`/`.litematic`/`.schem`/`.mcstructure`into raw-centric`.crn` | [ecosystem-interop §12.2](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/ecosystem-interop/) |
| `cairn info <file.crn> --editions java,bedrock` | Report registry compatibility window, semantic-sensitive members, and recommended test targets | [versioning-editions §10.5](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/versioning-editions/) |
| `cairn diff-blocks <schematic> <file.crn>` | Voxel XOR + state diff for the self-correction loop | [ecosystem-interop §12.2](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/ecosystem-interop/),[evaluation](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/evaluation/) |

## Targeting rules

Per [compilation §4.2](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/compilation/):

- `--edition`is- **required**for any subcommand that emits voxels. The same- `1.21`means different things on Java and Bedrock, and Java's DataVersion is unrelated to Bedrock's- `block_version`.
- `--target`accepts either the legacy semver form (- `1.21.4`) or a date-based string; both are resolved through DataVersion as the canonical ordering key (- [versioning-editions §10.1](https://cairn.kage1020.com/spec/versioning-editions/)).

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE).

# polymarket_client_sdk_v2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/polymarket_client_sdk_v2/0.6.0/polymarket_client_sdk_v2/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#polymarket-rust-client)Polymarket Rust Client

An ergonomic Rust client for interacting with Polymarket services, primarily the Central Limit Order Book (CLOB).
This crate provides strongly typed request builders, authenticated endpoints, `alloy` support and more.

[§](https://docs.rs#table-of-contents)Table of Contents

- [Overview](https://docs.rs#overview)
- [Getting Started](https://docs.rs#getting-started)
- [Feature Flags](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)
- [Re-exported Types](https://docs.rs#re-exported-types)
- [Examples](https://docs.rs#examples)
- [Additional CLOB Capabilities](https://docs.rs#additional-clob-capabilities)
- [Setting Token Allowances](https://docs.rs#token-allowances)
- [Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv)
- [Contributing](https://docs.rs#contributing)
- [About Polymarket](https://docs.rs#about-polymarket)

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

- **Typed CLOB requests**(orders, trades, markets, balances, and more)
- **Dual authentication flows**- Normal authenticated flow
- [Builder](https://docs.polymarket.com/developers/builders/builder-intro)authentication flow

- **Type-level state machine**- Prevents using authenticated endpoints before authenticating
- Compile-time enforcement of correct transitions

- **Signer support**via- `alloy::signers::Signer`- Including remote signers, e.g. AWS KMS

- **Zero-cost abstractions**— no dynamic dispatch in hot paths
- **Order builders**for easy construction & signing
- **Full**- `serde`support
- **Async-first design**with- `reqwest`

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

Add the crate to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
polymarket_client_sdk_v2 = "0.6"
```
or

`cargo add polymarket_client_sdk_v2`Then run any of the examples

`cargo run --example unauthenticated`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

The crate is modular with optional features for different Polymarket APIs:

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| `clob` | Core CLOB client for order placement, market data, and authentication |
| `tracing` | Structured logging via for HTTP requests, auth flows, and caching`tracing` |
| `ws` | WebSocket client for real-time orderbook, price, and user event streaming |
| `rtds` | Real-time data streams for crypto prices (Binance, Chainlink) and comments |
| `data` | Data API client for positions, trades, leaderboards, and analytics |
| `gamma` | Gamma API client for market/event discovery, search, and metadata |
| `bridge` | Bridge API client for cross-chain deposits (EVM, Solana, Bitcoin) |
| `rfq` | RFQ API (within CLOB) for submitting and querying quotes |
| `heartbeats` | Clob feature that automatically sends heartbeat messages to the Polymarket server, if the client disconnects all open orders will be cancelled |
| `ctf` | CTF API client to perform split/merge/redeem on binary and neg risk markets |

Enable features in your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
polymarket_client_sdk_v2 = { version = "0.6", features = ["ws", "data"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#re-exported-types)Re-exported Types

This SDK re-exports commonly used types from external crates so you don’t need to add them to your `Cargo.toml`:

[§](https://docs.rs#from-types-module)From `types` module

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::{
    Address, ChainId, Signature, address,  // from alloy::primitives
    DateTime, NaiveDate, Utc,              // from chrono
    Decimal, dec,                          // from rust_decimal + rust_decimal_macros
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#from-auth-module)From `auth` module

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::auth::{
    LocalSigner, Signer,          // from alloy::signers (LocalSigner + trait)
    Uuid, ApiKey,                 // from uuid (ApiKey = Uuid)
    SecretString, ExposeSecret,   // from secrecy
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#from-error-module)From `error` module

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::error::{
    StatusCode, Method,           // from reqwest (for error inspection)
};
```
This allows you to work with the SDK without managing version compatibility for these common dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

See `examples/` for the complete set. Below are hand-picked examples for common use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#clob-client)CLOB Client

[§](https://docs.rs#unauthenticated-client-read-only)Unauthenticated client (read-only)

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::Client;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let client = Client::default();
    let ok = client.ok().await?;
    println!("Ok: {ok}");
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#authenticated-client)Authenticated client

Set `POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY` as an environment variable with your private key.

If using MetaMask or hardware wallet, you must first set token allowances. See [Token Allowances](https://docs.rs#token-allowances) section below.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use std::str::FromStr as _;
use alloy::signers::Signer as _;
use alloy::signers::local::LocalSigner;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::{POLYGON, PRIVATE_KEY_VAR};
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::{Client, Config};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let private_key = std::env::var(PRIVATE_KEY_VAR).expect("Need a private key");
    let signer = LocalSigner::from_str(&private_key)?.with_chain_id(Some(POLYGON));
    let client = Client::new("https://clob-v2.polymarket.com", Config::default())?
        .authentication_builder(&signer)
        .authenticate()
        .await?;
    let ok = client.ok().await?;
    println!("Ok: {ok}");
    let api_keys = client.api_keys().await?;
    println!("API keys: {api_keys:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#proxysafe-wallets)Proxy/Safe wallets

For proxy/Safe wallets, the funder address is **automatically derived** using CREATE2 from your signer’s EOA address:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let client = Client::new("https://clob-v2.polymarket.com", Config::default())?
    .authentication_builder(&signer)
    .signature_type(SignatureType::GnosisSafe)  // Funder auto-derived via CREATE2
    .authenticate()
    .await?;
```
The SDK computes the deterministic wallet address that Polymarket deploys for your EOA. This is the same address shown on polymarket.com when you log in with a browser wallet.

If you need to override the derived address (e.g., for advanced use cases), you can explicitly provide it:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let client = Client::new("https://clob-v2.polymarket.com", Config::default())?
    .authentication_builder(&signer)
    .funder(address!("<your-polymarket-wallet-address>"))
    .signature_type(SignatureType::GnosisSafe)
    .authenticate()
    .await?;
```
You can also derive these addresses manually:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::{derive_safe_wallet, derive_proxy_wallet, POLYGON};
// For browser wallet users (GnosisSafe)
let safe_address = derive_safe_wallet(signer.address(), POLYGON);
// For Magic/email wallet users (Proxy)
let proxy_address = derive_proxy_wallet(signer.address(), POLYGON);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#funder-address)Funder Address

The **funder address** is the actual address that holds your funds on Polymarket. When using proxy wallets (email wallets
like Magic or browser extension wallets), the signing key differs from the address holding the funds. The SDK automatically
derives the correct funder address using CREATE2 when you specify `SignatureType::Proxy` or `SignatureType::GnosisSafe`.
You can override this with `.funder(address)` if needed.

[§](https://docs.rs#signature-types)Signature Types

The **signature_type** parameter tells the system how to verify your signatures:

- `signature_type=0`(default): Standard EOA (Externally Owned Account) signatures - includes MetaMask, hardware wallets, and any wallet where you control the private key directly
- `signature_type=1`: Email/Magic wallet signatures (delegated signing)
- `signature_type=2`: Browser wallet proxy signatures (when using a proxy contract, not direct wallet connections)
- `signature_type=3`: EIP-1271 smart contract wallet signatures (- **V2 orders only**)

See [ SignatureType](https://docs.rs/src/clob/types/mod.rs) for more information.

For deposit wallets, pass the deployed deposit wallet as the funder and use `SignatureType::Poly1271`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let client = Client::new("https://clob-v2.polymarket.com", Config::default())?
    .authentication_builder(&signer)
    .funder(deposit_wallet)
    .signature_type(SignatureType::Poly1271)
    .authenticate()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#place-a-market-order)Place a market order

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use std::str::FromStr as _;
use alloy::signers::Signer as _;
use alloy::signers::local::LocalSigner;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::{POLYGON, PRIVATE_KEY_VAR};
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::{Client, Config};
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::types::{Amount, OrderType, Side};
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::Decimal;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let private_key = std::env::var(PRIVATE_KEY_VAR).expect("Need a private key");
    let signer = LocalSigner::from_str(&private_key)?.with_chain_id(Some(POLYGON));
    let client = Client::new("https://clob-v2.polymarket.com", Config::default())?
        .authentication_builder(&signer)
        .authenticate()
        .await?;
    let order = client
        .market_order()
        .token_id("<token-id>")
        .amount(Amount::usdc(Decimal::ONE_HUNDRED)?)
        .side(Side::Buy)
        .order_type(OrderType::FOK)
        .build()
        .await?;
    let signed_order = client.sign(&signer, order).await?;
    let response = client.post_order(signed_order).await?;
    println!("Order response: {:?}", response);
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#place-a-limit-order)Place a limit order

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use std::str::FromStr as _;
use alloy::signers::Signer as _;
use alloy::signers::local::LocalSigner;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::{POLYGON, PRIVATE_KEY_VAR};
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::{Client, Config};
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::types::Side;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::Decimal;
use rust_decimal_macros::dec;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let private_key = std::env::var(PRIVATE_KEY_VAR).expect("Need a private key");
    let signer = LocalSigner::from_str(&private_key)?.with_chain_id(Some(POLYGON));
    let client = Client::new("https://clob-v2.polymarket.com", Config::default())?
        .authentication_builder(&signer)
        .authenticate()
        .await?;
    let order = client
        .limit_order()
        .token_id("<token-id>")
        .size(Decimal::ONE_HUNDRED)
        .price(dec!(0.1))
        .side(Side::Buy)
        .build()
        .await?;
    let signed_order = client.sign(&signer, order).await?;
    let response = client.post_order(signed_order).await?;
    println!("Order response: {:?}", response);
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#v1-and-v2-protocols)V1 and V2 protocols

The SDK supports both V1 (legacy) and V2 exchange contracts. Protocol is **auto-detected** on
the first order build via `GET /version` and cached for the lifetime of the `Client`. You pick
the protocol by pointing the client at the corresponding host:

| Protocol | Host | Collateral | EIP-712 domain version |
|---|---|---|---|
| V2 | `https://clob-v2.polymarket.com` | pUSD | `"2"` |
| V1 | `https://clob.polymarket.com` | USDC.e | `"1"` |

V2 orders add `timestamp`, `metadata`, and `builder` fields. V1 orders use `taker`, `nonce`,
and `feeRateBps` instead. The order builder exposes both sets of fields — the ones that don’t
apply to the detected protocol are silently ignored at build time, so you can write one
code-path that works against either server.

V2-specific builder fields (ignored when the server runs V1):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::B256;
let order = client
    .limit_order()
    .token_id("<token-id>")
    .size(Decimal::ONE_HUNDRED)
    .price(dec!(0.5))
    .side(Side::Buy)
    .metadata(B256::ZERO)           // 32 bytes of custom metadata
    .builder_code(B256::ZERO)       // builder fee attribution
    .defer_exec(false)              // defer execution
    .build()
    .await?;
```
V1-specific builder fields (ignored when the server runs V2):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::Address;
let order = client
    .limit_order()
    .token_id("<token-id>")
    .size(Decimal::ONE_HUNDRED)
    .price(dec!(0.5))
    .side(Side::Buy)
    .taker(Address::ZERO)           // explicit taker; default zero = public order
    .nonce(0)                       // on-chain cancel nonce; default 0
    .fee_rate_bps(0)                // must match the market rate when set
    .build()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#builder-attributed-trading)Builder-attributed trading

In V2, builder attribution is carried on the order’s `builder_code` field (and as a
query parameter on `builder_trades`). Set a default `builder_code` on the [`Config`] and
every order constructed via [`Client::limit_order`] / [`Client::market_order`] inherits
it unless overridden.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use std::str::FromStr as _;
use alloy::signers::Signer as _;
use alloy::signers::local::LocalSigner;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::{Client, Config};
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::types::request::TradesRequest;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::B256;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::{POLYGON, PRIVATE_KEY_VAR};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let private_key = std::env::var(PRIVATE_KEY_VAR).expect("Need a private key");
    let builder_code = B256::from_str(&std::env::var("POLYMARKET_BUILDER_CODE")?)?;
    let signer = LocalSigner::from_str(&private_key)?.with_chain_id(Some(POLYGON));
    let config = Config::builder().builder_code(builder_code).build();
    let client = Client::new("https://clob-v2.polymarket.com", config)?
        .authentication_builder(&signer)
        .authenticate()
        .await?;
    // Orders built below will carry the configured `builder_code`.
    let builder_trades = client
        .builder_trades(builder_code, &TradesRequest::default(), None)
        .await?;
    println!("Builder trades: {builder_trades:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#websocket-streaming)WebSocket Streaming

Real-time orderbook and user event streaming. Requires the `ws` feature.

`polymarket_client_sdk_v2 = { version = "0.6", features = ["ws"] }`[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use std::str::FromStr as _;
use futures::StreamExt as _;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::clob::ws::Client;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::U256;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let client = Client::default();
    // Subscribe to orderbook updates for specific assets.
    let asset_ids = vec![U256::from_str("<asset-id>")?];
    let stream = client.subscribe_orderbook(asset_ids)?;
    let mut stream = Box::pin(stream);
    while let Some(book_result) = stream.next().await {
        let book = book_result?;
        println!(
            "Orderbook update for {}: {} bids, {} asks",
            book.asset_id, book.bids.len(), book.asks.len()
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
Available streams:

- `subscribe_orderbook()`- Bid/ask levels for assets
- `subscribe_prices()`- Price change events
- `subscribe_midpoints()`- Calculated midpoint prices
- `subscribe_orders()`- User order updates (authenticated)
- `subscribe_trades()`- User trade executions (authenticated)

See [ examples/clob/ws/](https://docs.rs/examples/clob/ws/) for more WebSocket examples including authenticated user streams.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-apis)Optional APIs

[§](https://docs.rs#data-api)Data API

Trading analytics, positions, and leaderboards. Requires the `data` feature.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::data::Client;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::data::types::request::PositionsRequest;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::address;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let client = Client::default();
    let user = address!("0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"); // Your address
    let request = PositionsRequest::builder().user(user).limit(10)?.build();
    let positions = client.positions(&request).await?;
    println!("Open positions: {:?}", positions);
    Ok(())
}
```
See [ examples/data.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/data.rs) for trades, leaderboards, activity, and more.

[§](https://docs.rs#gamma-api)Gamma API

Market and event discovery. Requires the `gamma` feature.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::gamma::Client;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::gamma::types::request::{EventsRequest, SearchRequest};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let client = Client::default();
    // Find active events
    let request = EventsRequest::builder().active(true).limit(5).build();
    let events = client.events(&request).await?;
    println!("Found {} events", events.len());
    // Search for markets
    let search = SearchRequest::builder().q("bitcoin").build();
    let results = client.search(&search).await?;
    println!("Search results: {:?}", results);
    Ok(())
}
```
See [ examples/gamma.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/gamma/client.rs) for tags, series, comments, and sports endpoints.

[§](https://docs.rs#bridge-api)Bridge API

Cross-chain deposits from EVM chains, Solana, and Bitcoin. Requires the `bridge` feature.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::bridge::Client;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::bridge::types::DepositRequest;
use polymarket_client_sdk_v2::types::address;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let client = Client::default();
    // Get deposit addresses for your wallet
    let request = DepositRequest::builder()
        .address(address!("0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000")) // Your address
        .build();
    let response = client.deposit(&request).await?;
    println!("EVM: {}", response.address.evm);
    println!("Solana: {}", response.address.svm);
    println!("Bitcoin: {}", response.address.btc);
    Ok(())
}
```
See [ examples/bridge.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/bridge.rs) for supported assets and minimum deposits.

[§](https://docs.rs#additional-clob-capabilities)Additional CLOB Capabilities

Beyond basic order placement, the CLOB client supports:

- **Rewards & Earnings**- Query maker rewards, daily earnings, and reward percentages
- **Streaming Pagination**-- `stream_data()`for iterating through large result sets
- **Batch Operations**-- `post_orders()`and- `cancel_orders()`for multiple orders at once
- **Order Scoring**- Check if orders qualify for maker rewards
- **Notifications**- Manage trading notifications
- **Balance Management**- Query and refresh balance/allowance caches
- **Geoblock Detection**- Check if trading is available in your region

See [ examples/clob/authenticated.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/clob/authenticated.rs) for comprehensive usage.

[§](https://docs.rs#token-allowances)Token Allowances

[§](https://docs.rs#do-i-need-to-set-allowances)Do I need to set allowances?

MetaMask and EOA users must set token allowances.
If you are using a proxy or [Safe](https://help.safe.global/en/articles/40869-what-is-safe)-type wallet, then you do not.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-are-allowances)What are allowances?

Think of allowances as permissions. Before Polymarket can move your funds to execute trades, you need to give the exchange contracts permission to access your USDC and conditional tokens.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-setup)Quick Setup

You need to approve two types of tokens:

- **USDC**(for deposits and trading)
- **Conditional Tokens**(the outcome tokens you trade)

Each needs approval for the exchange contracts to work properly.

[§](https://docs.rs#setting-allowances)Setting Allowances

Use [examples/approvals.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/approvals.rs) to approve the right contracts. Run once to approve USDC. Then change
the `TOKEN_TO_APPROVE` and run for each conditional token.

**Pro tip**: You only need to set these once per wallet. After that, you can trade freely.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv)Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

**MSRV: Rust  1.88**

Older versions *may* compile, but are not supported.

This project aims to maintain compatibility with a Rust version that is at least six months old.

Version updates may occur more frequently than the policy guideline states if external forces require it. For example, a CVE in a downstream dependency requiring an MSRV bump would be considered an acceptable reason to violate the six-month guideline.

[§](https://docs.rs#contributing)Contributing

We encourage contributions from the community. Check out our [contributing guidelines](https://docs.rs/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) for
instructions on how to contribute to this SDK.

[§](https://docs.rs#about-polymarket)About Polymarket

[Polymarket](https://docs.polymarket.com/polymarket-learn/get-started/what-is-polymarket) is the world’s largest prediction market, allowing you to stay informed and profit from your knowledge by
betting on future events across various topics.
Studies show prediction markets are often more accurate than pundits because they combine news, polls, and expert
opinions into a single value that represents the market’s view of an event’s odds. Our markets reflect accurate, unbiased,
and real-time probabilities for the events that matter most to you. Markets seek truth.

# gdscript_scene - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-scene/0.5.3/gdscript_scene/

## Expand description

`gdscript-scene` — a `.tscn`/`.tres` **text** parser for scene-aware analysis (Phase 4).

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Godot’s text scene format is INI-like: bracketed section headers (`[node …]`, `[ext_resource …]`,
…) followed by `key = value` property lines. This crate parses that structure — node names,
types, parent paths, attached scripts, `unique_name_in_owner`, and instanced sub-scenes — into a
`SceneModel`**with byte spans**, so the type layer (Phase-4 M1+) can resolve `$Path` /
`%Unique` / `get_node("…")` to a node’s real `Control`/`Node` subclass instead of bare `Node` —
intelligence the Godot editor’s own LSP produces only in-editor and never flows into inference.

**M0 scope:** the pure, wasm-clean [ parse_scene](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scene.html) (

`&str -> SceneModel`) + the model + byte
spans. It **records**the typing inputs (

`type=`/`script=`/`instance=`); it does **not**resolve a

`Ty` (M1), recurse into instanced sub-scenes, build the project-wide script↔scene index, or
cache via salsa (M1+). See `plans/PHASE-4-M0-PLAYBOOK.md`.**Invariant:** the parser is strictly additive and **never fails** — every binary/malformed/
unknown form degrades to an empty-or-partial model + a [ SceneProblem](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneProblem.html), never a panic or

`Err`.
The floor is always parity with the engine’s `Node`-everywhere baseline.**Portability:** a core crate — wasm32-clean (no `std::fs`, no `Instant`, no threads); `.tscn`
text is injected via the VFS exactly like `.gd`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [ExtId](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtId.html)
- An `ext_resource`/`sub_resource`id — the opaque, quoted-string key as written (`"1"`,`"1_app"`,`"StyleBoxFlat_x"`). A 3.x bare-int id is normalized to its string form.
- [ExtResource](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtResource.html)
- An `[ext_resource …]`declaration.
- [NodeIdx](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeIdx.html)
- Index of a node into `SceneModel::nodes`
- [Node](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeProp.html)- Prop
- One body property line of a `[node …]`—`key = value`(value skipped). The key may be a bare identifier (an`@export`var or an engine property) or a`group/sub`override path.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneConnection.html)- Connection
- One `[connection …]`section — a signal wired to a method in the editor. The four spans are the**inner identifier**byte ranges (surrounding quotes excluded), so a rename rewrites exactly the name. A connection has no body.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneModel.html)- Model
- One parsed `.tscn`/`.tres`. Produced by`crate::parse_scene`**never**an`Err`— every malformed/binary/unknown form degrades to an empty-or-partial model plus a`SceneProblem``PartialEq`/`Eq`so it can be a backdated salsa query result (`Arc<SceneModel>`) in M1.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneNode.html)- Node
- One `[node …]`section: its header attributes + the two body properties we read.
- [SubResource](https://docs.rs/struct.SubResource.html)
- A `[sub_resource …]`declaration (type only — the value body is skipped).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Node](https://docs.rs/enum.NodePathResolution.html)- Path - Resolution
- The reason a node path did (not) resolve — for the `INVALID_NODE_PATH`decision (M2).
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneKind.html)- Kind
- Whether the parsed file is a `.tscn`scene (`gd_scene`) or a`.tres`resource (`gd_resource`).
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneProblem.html)- Problem
- A non-fatal problem found during parsing. The parser records these and keeps going — the floor
is always parity with the engine’s `Node`-everywhere baseline.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scene.html)- scene
- Parse `.tscn`/`.tres`text into a`SceneModel``Err`.

# cairn_lang_nbt - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cairn-lang-nbt/2026.7.2/cairn_lang_nbt/

## Expand description

NBT codec for the Cairn language.

Encodes Minecraft NBT in Java big-endian form (gzip-wrapped on disk).
Bedrock little-endian is a follow-up: the tag tree in [ tag](https://docs.rs/tag/index.html) is endian-
neutral so the Bedrock writer can grow alongside

`write_java_*` without
a second tree type.Used by `cairn-lang-formats` for the various schematic/structure file
formats. The CLI never reaches in directly — it talks to format helpers
which talk to this crate.

# sqlglot_rust - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sqlglot-rust/0.10.8/sqlglot_rust/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#sqlglot-rust)sqlglot-rust

A SQL parser, optimizer, and transpiler library written in Rust,
inspired by Python’s [sqlglot](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot).

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Parse SQL strings into a structured AST
- Generate SQL from AST nodes
- Transpile between SQL dialects (30 dialects including MySQL, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, DuckDB, Hive, Spark, Presto, Trino, T-SQL, Oracle, ClickHouse, Redshift, and more)
- Optimize SQL queries
- CTEs, subqueries, UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT
- Window functions, CAST, EXTRACT, EXISTS
- Pretty-print SQL output
- AST traversal (walk, find, transform)
- AST diff for semantic SQL comparison

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use sqlglot_rust::{parse, generate, transpile, Dialect};
// Parse a SQL query
let ast = parse("SELECT a, b FROM t WHERE a > 1", Dialect::Ansi).unwrap();
// Generate SQL for a specific dialect
let sql = generate(&ast, Dialect::Postgres);
assert_eq!(sql, "SELECT a, b FROM t WHERE a > 1");
// One-step transpile between dialects
let result = transpile("SELECT a, b FROM t", Dialect::Ansi, Dialect::Postgres).unwrap();
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# gdscript_syntax - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-syntax/0.5.3/gdscript_syntax/

## Expand description

`gdscript-syntax` — lexer + indentation pre-pass + lossless parser for GDScript.

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Phase 1 fills this in: a `logos` lexer, a hand-written indentation pre-pass
(INDENT/DEDENT/NEWLINE), and a hand-written recursive-descent parser producing a
lossless [ cstree](https://docs.rs/cstree/0.14.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cstree/index.html) CST plus a typed AST, behind a

`Parser` trait
(tree-sitter-gdscript is the differential test oracle, never the
grammar-of-record — see ADR-0002).The crate “knows nothing about salsa or LSP” (rust-analyzer’s `syntax` layer):
it is pure text → tree. It must build for `wasm32` — no `std::fs`, no clocks, no
threads.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)
- WS4 — the typed AST.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Indent](https://docs.rs/struct.IndentDiagnostic.html)- Diagnostic
- An indentation diagnostic produced while injecting block-structure markers.
Byte-ranged; mapped into a `gdscript-base``Diagnostic`by the IDE layer.
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.Parse.html)
- The result of parsing a source file: a lossless green tree, the interner needed to read token text back, and the diagnostics gathered while parsing.
- [RawToken](https://docs.rs/struct.RawToken.html)
- A lexed token: its `SyntaxKind`
- [Syntax](https://docs.rs/struct.SyntaxError.html)- Error
- A byte-ranged syntax diagnostic with an “expected X” style message.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Syntax](https://docs.rs/enum.SyntaxKind.html)- Kind
- Every terminal and non-terminal kind in the GDScript syntax tree.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Parse GDScript source into a lossless `Parse`
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_prepass.html)- prepass
- Inject `Newline`/`Indent`/`Dedent`markers into the lexer token stream.
- [tokenize](https://docs.rs/fn.tokenize.html)
- Lex `src`into a lossless`RawToken``SyntaxKind::Error`

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [GdNode](https://docs.rs/type.GdNode.html)
- A resolved (interner-carrying) red node — supports `Display`/`.text()`and the byte-exact round-trip. This is the public tree type for callers that need text.
- [GdToken](https://docs.rs/type.GdToken.html)
- A resolved red token.
- [Syntax](https://docs.rs/type.SyntaxNode.html)- Node
- A bare (resolver-less) red node — cheap, `Send + Sync`; text needs a resolver.

# cairn_lang_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cairn-lang-core/2026.7.2/cairn_lang_core/

## Expand description

Core of the Cairn language.

Hosts the surface-syntax lexer, parser, and AST, the Intent IR — the
first semantic layer above the surface, where struct/site/def bodies are
reorganised into typed members with roles — and the diagnostic-collecting
`check` pipeline that turns structural surprises in a lowered module into
position-anchored [ check::Diagnostic](https://docs.rs/check/struct.Diagnostic.html) values. Registry-backed lifting
(materials, themes, per-edition blockstate) lives in downstream layers.

# gdscript_api - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-api/0.5.3/gdscript_api/

## Expand description

`gdscript-api` — the Godot engine model, generated from `extension_api.json`.

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

The model (engine classes + inheritance chain, methods, properties, signals, enums,
constants, singletons, utility functions, builtin Variant types) plus the hand-authored
GDScript layer the dump omits (pseudo-constants + builtin functions). See
`plans/PHASE-2-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAYBOOK.md` §4.

[§](https://docs.rs#shape)Shape

[ model::ApiData](https://docs.rs/model/struct.ApiData.html) is the serializable root that

`xtask codegen-api` `rkyv`-encodes into a
binary blob; [deserializes it once, rebuilds the name indices, merges the hand-authored layer, and exposes the lookup API (](https://docs.rs/struct.EngineApi.html)

`EngineApi``lookup.rs`). The model is `Arc`-shared
and excluded from per-file timing, so the one-time deserialize is amortized.[§](https://docs.rs#targets)Targets

Native builds embed the blob via `include_bytes!` ([ bundled](https://docs.rs/fn.bundled.html), behind the default

`bundled-api` feature). The crate never touches `std::fs`/clocks/threads, so it builds for
`wasm32`; there the blob is **not**embedded (Playbook §4.5) — the host fetches it and calls

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.EngineApi.html#method.from_bytes)

`EngineApi::from_bytes`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# unicode_bidi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicode-bidi/latest/unicode_bidi/

## Expand description

This crate implements the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/) for display of mixed
right-to-left and left-to-right text.  It is written in safe Rust, compatible with the
current stable release.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use unicode_bidi::BidiInfo;
// This example text is defined using `concat!` because some browsers
// and text editors have trouble displaying bidi strings.
let text = concat![
  "א",
  "ב",
  "ג",
  "a",
  "b",
  "c",
];
// Resolve embedding levels within the text.  Pass `None` to detect the
// paragraph level automatically.
let bidi_info = BidiInfo::new(&text, None);
// This paragraph has embedding level 1 because its first strong character is RTL.
assert_eq!(bidi_info.paragraphs.len(), 1);
let para = &bidi_info.paragraphs[0];
assert_eq!(para.level.number(), 1);
assert_eq!(para.level.is_rtl(), true);
// Re-ordering is done after wrapping each paragraph into a sequence of
// lines. For this example, I'll just use a single line that spans the
// entire paragraph.
let line = para.range.clone();
let display = bidi_info.reorder_line(para, line);
assert_eq!(display, concat![
  "a",
  "b",
  "c",
  "ג",
  "ב",
  "א",
]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `std`: Enabled by default, but can be disabled to make- `unicode_bidi`- `#![no_std]`+- `alloc`compatible.
- `hardcoded-data`: Enabled by default. Includes hardcoded Unicode bidi data and more convenient APIs.
- `serde`: Adds [- `serde::Serialize`] and [- `serde::Deserialize`] implementations to relevant types.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::data_source::`- [BidiDataSource](https://docs.rs/data_source/trait.BidiDataSource.html);
- `pub use crate::level::`- [Level](https://docs.rs/level/struct.Level.html);
- `pub use crate::level::`- [LTR_LEVEL](https://docs.rs/level/constant.LTR_LEVEL.html);
- `pub use crate::level::`- [RTL_LEVEL](https://docs.rs/level/constant.RTL_LEVEL.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [data_](https://docs.rs/data_source/index.html)- source
- [deprecated](https://docs.rs/deprecated/index.html)
- This module holds deprecated assets only.
- [format_](https://docs.rs/format_chars/index.html)- chars
- Directional Formatting Characters
- [level](https://docs.rs/level/index.html)
- Bidi Embedding Level
- [utf16](https://docs.rs/utf16/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiInfo.html)- Info
- Bidi information of the text.
- [Hardcoded](https://docs.rs/struct.HardcodedBidiData.html)- Bidi - Data
- Hardcoded Bidi data that ships with the unicode-bidi crate.
- [Initial](https://docs.rs/struct.InitialInfo.html)- Info
- Initial bidi information of the text.
- [Paragraph](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html)
- Contains a reference of `BidiInfo`and one of its`paragraphs`. And it supports all operation in the`Paragraph`that needs also its`BidiInfo`such as`direction`.
- [Paragraph](https://docs.rs/struct.ParagraphBidiInfo.html)- Bidi - Info
- Bidi information of text treated as a single paragraph.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Text](https://docs.rs/trait.TextSource.html)- Source
- Trait that abstracts over a text source for use by the bidi algorithms.
We implement this for str (UTF-8) and for [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)(UTF-16, native-endian). (For internal unicode-bidi use; API may be unstable.) This trait is sealed and cannot be implemented for types outside this crate.

# unicode-bidi 0.3.18 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unicode-bidi/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# unicode_bidi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicode-bidi

## Expand description

This crate implements the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/) for display of mixed
right-to-left and left-to-right text.  It is written in safe Rust, compatible with the
current stable release.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use unicode_bidi::BidiInfo;
// This example text is defined using `concat!` because some browsers
// and text editors have trouble displaying bidi strings.
let text = concat![
  "א",
  "ב",
  "ג",
  "a",
  "b",
  "c",
];
// Resolve embedding levels within the text.  Pass `None` to detect the
// paragraph level automatically.
let bidi_info = BidiInfo::new(&text, None);
// This paragraph has embedding level 1 because its first strong character is RTL.
assert_eq!(bidi_info.paragraphs.len(), 1);
let para = &bidi_info.paragraphs[0];
assert_eq!(para.level.number(), 1);
assert_eq!(para.level.is_rtl(), true);
// Re-ordering is done after wrapping each paragraph into a sequence of
// lines. For this example, I'll just use a single line that spans the
// entire paragraph.
let line = para.range.clone();
let display = bidi_info.reorder_line(para, line);
assert_eq!(display, concat![
  "a",
  "b",
  "c",
  "ג",
  "ב",
  "א",
]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `std`: Enabled by default, but can be disabled to make- `unicode_bidi`- `#![no_std]`+- `alloc`compatible.
- `hardcoded-data`: Enabled by default. Includes hardcoded Unicode bidi data and more convenient APIs.
- `serde`: Adds [- `serde::Serialize`] and [- `serde::Deserialize`] implementations to relevant types.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::data_source::`- [BidiDataSource](https://docs.rs/data_source/trait.BidiDataSource.html);
- `pub use crate::level::`- [Level](https://docs.rs/level/struct.Level.html);
- `pub use crate::level::`- [LTR_LEVEL](https://docs.rs/level/constant.LTR_LEVEL.html);
- `pub use crate::level::`- [RTL_LEVEL](https://docs.rs/level/constant.RTL_LEVEL.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [data_](https://docs.rs/data_source/index.html)- source
- [deprecated](https://docs.rs/deprecated/index.html)
- This module holds deprecated assets only.
- [format_](https://docs.rs/format_chars/index.html)- chars
- Directional Formatting Characters
- [level](https://docs.rs/level/index.html)
- Bidi Embedding Level
- [utf16](https://docs.rs/utf16/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiInfo.html)- Info
- Bidi information of the text.
- [Hardcoded](https://docs.rs/struct.HardcodedBidiData.html)- Bidi - Data
- Hardcoded Bidi data that ships with the unicode-bidi crate.
- [Initial](https://docs.rs/struct.InitialInfo.html)- Info
- Initial bidi information of the text.
- [Paragraph](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html)
- Contains a reference of `BidiInfo`and one of its`paragraphs`. And it supports all operation in the`Paragraph`that needs also its`BidiInfo`such as`direction`.
- [Paragraph](https://docs.rs/struct.ParagraphBidiInfo.html)- Bidi - Info
- Bidi information of text treated as a single paragraph.
- [Paragraph](https://docs.rs/struct.ParagraphInfo.html)- Info
- Bidi information about a single paragraph
- [Utf8](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8IndexLenIter.html)- Index - LenIter
- Iterator over (UTF-8) string slices returning (index, char_len) tuple.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/enum.BidiClass.html)- Class
- Represents values of the Unicode character property
`Bidi_Class`*bidirectional character type*.
- [Direction](https://docs.rs/enum.Direction.html)

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [UNICODE_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNICODE_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- The [Unicode version](http://www.unicode.org/versions/)of data

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Text](https://docs.rs/trait.TextSource.html)- Source
- Trait that abstracts over a text source for use by the bidi algorithms.
We implement this for str (UTF-8) and for [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)(UTF-16, native-endian). (For internal unicode-bidi use; API may be unstable.) This trait is sealed and cannot be implemented for types outside this crate.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [bidi_](https://docs.rs/fn.bidi_class.html)- class
- Find the `BidiClass`of a single char.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_base_direction.html)- base_ - direction
- Get the base direction of the text provided according to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_base_direction_full.html)- base_ - direction_ - full
- Get the base direction of the text provided according to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm, considering the full text if the first paragraph is all-neutral.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_base_direction_full_with_data_source.html)- base_ - direction_ - full_ - with_ - data_ - source
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_base_direction_with_data_source.html)- base_ - direction_ - with_ - data_ - source

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Level](https://docs.rs/type.LevelRun.html)- Run
- A maximal substring of characters with the same embedding level.
- [Level](https://docs.rs/type.LevelRunVec.html)- RunVec

# lib.rs - source

# unicode_bidi/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)// Copyright 2015 The Servo Project Developers. See the
[2](https://docs.rs#2)// COPYRIGHT file at the top-level directory of this distribution.
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//
[4](https://docs.rs#4)// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 <LICENSE-APACHE or
[5](https://docs.rs#5)// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0> or the MIT license
[6](https://docs.rs#6)// <LICENSE-MIT or http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT>, at your
[7](https://docs.rs#7)// option. This file may not be copied, modified, or distributed
[8](https://docs.rs#8)// except according to those terms.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! This crate implements the [Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm][tr9] for display of mixed
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! right-to-left and left-to-right text.  It is written in safe Rust, compatible with the
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! current stable release.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! ## Example
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! ```rust
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! # #[cfg(feature = "hardcoded-data")] {
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! use unicode_bidi::BidiInfo;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! // This example text is defined using `concat!` because some browsers
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! // and text editors have trouble displaying bidi strings.
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! let text = concat![
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!   "א",
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!   "ב",
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!   "ג",
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!   "a",
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!   "b",
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!   "c",
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! ];
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! // Resolve embedding levels within the text.  Pass `None` to detect the
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! // paragraph level automatically.
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! let bidi_info = BidiInfo::new(&text, None);
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! // This paragraph has embedding level 1 because its first strong character is RTL.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! assert_eq!(bidi_info.paragraphs.len(), 1);
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! let para = &bidi_info.paragraphs[0];
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! assert_eq!(para.level.number(), 1);
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! assert_eq!(para.level.is_rtl(), true);
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! // Re-ordering is done after wrapping each paragraph into a sequence of
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! // lines. For this example, I'll just use a single line that spans the
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! // entire paragraph.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! let line = para.range.clone();
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! let display = bidi_info.reorder_line(para, line);
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! assert_eq!(display, concat![
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!   "a",
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!   "b",
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!   "c",
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!   "ג",
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!   "ב",
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!   "א",
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! ]);
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! # } // feature = "hardcoded-data"
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! ```
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! # Features
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! - `std`: Enabled by default, but can be disabled to make `unicode_bidi`
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!   `#![no_std]` + `alloc` compatible.
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! - `hardcoded-data`: Enabled by default. Includes hardcoded Unicode bidi data and more convenient APIs.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! - `serde`: Adds [`serde::Serialize`] and [`serde::Deserialize`]
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!   implementations to relevant types.
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! [tr9]: <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/>
[67](https://docs.rs#67)
[68](https://docs.rs#68)#![no_std]

[73](https://docs.rs#73)extern crate alloc;

[109](https://docs.rs#109)
[110](https://docs.rs#110)/// Trait that abstracts over a text source for use by the bidi algorithms.
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// We implement this for str (UTF-8) and for [u16] (UTF-16, native-endian).
[112](https://docs.rs#112)/// (For internal unicode-bidi use; API may be unstable.)
[113](https://docs.rs#113)/// This trait is sealed and cannot be implemented for types outside this crate.
[114](https://docs.rs#114)pub trait TextSource<'text>: private::Sealed {
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    type CharIter: Iterator<Item = char>;
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    type CharIndexIter: Iterator<Item = (usize, char)>;
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    type IndexLenIter: Iterator<Item = (usize, usize)>;
[118](https://docs.rs#118)
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    /// Return the length of the text in code units.
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    #[doc(hidden)]
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    fn len(&self) -> usize;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    /// Get the character at a given code unit index, along with its length in code units.
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    /// Returns None if index is out of range, or points inside a multi-code-unit character.
[125](https://docs.rs#125)    /// Returns REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER for any unpaired surrogates in UTF-16.
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    #[doc(hidden)]
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    fn char_at(&self, index: usize) -> Option<(char, usize)>;
[128](https://docs.rs#128)
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    /// Return a subrange of the text, indexed by code units.
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    /// (We don't implement all of the Index trait, just the minimum we use.)
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    #[doc(hidden)]
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    fn subrange(&self, range: Range<usize>) -> &Self;
[133](https://docs.rs#133)
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    /// An iterator over the text returning Unicode characters,
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    /// REPLACEMENT_CHAR for invalid code units.
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    #[doc(hidden)]
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    fn chars(&'text self) -> Self::CharIter;
[138](https://docs.rs#138)
[139](https://docs.rs#139)    /// An iterator over the text returning (index, char) tuples,
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    /// where index is the starting code-unit index of the character,
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    /// and char is its Unicode value (or REPLACEMENT_CHAR if invalid).
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    #[doc(hidden)]
[143](https://docs.rs#143)    fn char_indices(&'text self) -> Self::CharIndexIter;
[144](https://docs.rs#144)
[145](https://docs.rs#145)    /// An iterator over the text returning (index, length) tuples,
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    /// where index is the starting code-unit index of the character,
[147](https://docs.rs#147)    /// and length is its length in code units.
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    #[doc(hidden)]
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    fn indices_lengths(&'text self) -> Self::IndexLenIter;
[150](https://docs.rs#150)
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    /// Number of code units the given character uses.
[152](https://docs.rs#152)    #[doc(hidden)]
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    fn char_len(ch: char) -> usize;
[154](https://docs.rs#154)}
[155](https://docs.rs#155)
[156](https://docs.rs#156)mod private {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    pub trait Sealed {}
[158](https://docs.rs#158)
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    // Implement for str and [u16] only.
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    impl Sealed for str {}
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    impl Sealed for [u16] {}
[162](https://docs.rs#162)}
[163](https://docs.rs#163)

[166](https://docs.rs#166)    Ltr,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    Rtl,
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    Mixed,
[169](https://docs.rs#169)}

[173](https://docs.rs#173)pub struct ParagraphInfo {
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    /// The paragraphs boundaries within the text, as byte indices.
[175](https://docs.rs#175)    ///
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// TODO: Shrink this to only include the starting index?
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    pub range: Range<usize>,
[178](https://docs.rs#178)
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    /// The paragraph embedding level.
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    ///
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    /// <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#BD4>
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    pub level: Level,
[183](https://docs.rs#183)}
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)impl ParagraphInfo {
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    /// Gets the length of the paragraph in the source text.
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
[188](https://docs.rs#188)        self.range.end - self.range.start
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    }
[190](https://docs.rs#190)}
[191](https://docs.rs#191)
[192](https://docs.rs#192)/// Initial bidi information of the text.
[193](https://docs.rs#193)///
[194](https://docs.rs#194)/// Contains the text paragraphs and `BidiClass` of its characters.
[195](https://docs.rs#195)#[derive(PartialEq, Debug)]
[196](https://docs.rs#196)pub struct InitialInfo<'text> {
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// The text
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    pub text: &'text str,
[199](https://docs.rs#199)
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// The BidiClass of the character at each byte in the text.
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// If a character is multiple bytes, its class will appear multiple times in the vector.
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    pub original_classes: Vec<BidiClass>,
[203](https://docs.rs#203)
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// The boundaries and level of each paragraph within the text.
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    pub paragraphs: Vec<ParagraphInfo>,
[206](https://docs.rs#206)}
[207](https://docs.rs#207)
[208](https://docs.rs#208)impl<'text> InitialInfo<'text> {
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// Find the paragraphs and BidiClasses in a string of text.
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    ///
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#The_Paragraph_Level>
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    ///
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// Also sets the class for each First Strong Isolate initiator (FSI) to LRI or RLI if a strong
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    /// character is found before the matching PDI.  If no strong character is found, the class will
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    /// remain FSI, and it's up to later stages to treat these as LRI when needed.
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    ///
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    /// The `hardcoded-data` Cargo feature (enabled by default) must be enabled to use this.
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    #[cfg(feature = "hardcoded-data")]
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    pub fn new(text: &str, default_para_level: Option<Level>) -> InitialInfo<'_> {
[221](https://docs.rs#221)        Self::new_with_data_source(&HardcodedBidiData, text, default_para_level)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    }
[223](https://docs.rs#223)
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// Find the paragraphs and BidiClasses in a string of text, with a custom [`BidiDataSource`]
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// for Bidi data. If you just wish to use the hardcoded Bidi data, please use [`InitialInfo::new()`]
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    /// instead (enabled with tbe default `hardcoded-data` Cargo feature)
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    ///
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    /// <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#The_Paragraph_Level>
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    ///
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    /// Also sets the class for each First Strong Isolate initiator (FSI) to LRI or RLI if a strong
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    /// character is found before the matching PDI.  If no strong character is found, the class will
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    /// remain FSI, and it's up to later stages to treat these as LRI when needed.
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    pub fn new_with_data_source<'a, D: BidiDataSource>(
[235](https://docs.rs#235)        data_source: &D,
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        text: &'a str,
[237](https://docs.rs#237)        default_para_level: Option<Level>,
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    ) -> InitialInfo<'a> {
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        InitialInfoExt::new_with_data_source(data_source, text, default_para_level).base
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    }
