[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)/// Extended version of InitialInfo (not public API).
[244](https://docs.rs#244)#[derive(PartialEq, Debug)]
[245](https://docs.rs#245)struct InitialInfoExt<'text> {
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    /// The base InitialInfo for the text, recording its paragraphs and bidi classes.
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    base: InitialInfo<'text>,
[248](https://docs.rs#248)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    /// Parallel to base.paragraphs, records whether each paragraph is "pure LTR" that
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// requires no further bidi processing (i.e. there are no RTL characters or bidi
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    /// control codes present), and whether any bidi isolation controls are present.
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    flags: Vec<ParagraphInfoFlags>,
[253](https://docs.rs#253)}
[254](https://docs.rs#254)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)#[derive(PartialEq, Debug)]
[256](https://docs.rs#256)struct ParagraphInfoFlags {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    is_pure_ltr: bool,
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    has_isolate_controls: bool,
[259](https://docs.rs#259)}
[260](https://docs.rs#260)
[261](https://docs.rs#261)impl<'text> InitialInfoExt<'text> {
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    /// Find the paragraphs and BidiClasses in a string of text, with a custom [`BidiDataSource`]
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// for Bidi data. If you just wish to use the hardcoded Bidi data, please use [`InitialInfo::new()`]
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    /// instead (enabled with tbe default `hardcoded-data` Cargo feature)
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    ///
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    /// <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#The_Paragraph_Level>
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    ///
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// Also sets the class for each First Strong Isolate initiator (FSI) to LRI or RLI if a strong
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// character is found before the matching PDI.  If no strong character is found, the class will
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// remain FSI, and it's up to later stages to treat these as LRI when needed.
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    pub fn new_with_data_source<'a, D: BidiDataSource>(
[273](https://docs.rs#273)        data_source: &D,
[274](https://docs.rs#274)        text: &'a str,
[275](https://docs.rs#275)        default_para_level: Option<Level>,
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    ) -> InitialInfoExt<'a> {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)        let mut paragraphs = Vec::<ParagraphInfo>::new();
[278](https://docs.rs#278)        let mut flags = Vec::<ParagraphInfoFlags>::new();
[279](https://docs.rs#279)        let (original_classes, _, _, _) = compute_initial_info(
[280](https://docs.rs#280)            data_source,
[281](https://docs.rs#281)            text,
[282](https://docs.rs#282)            default_para_level,
[283](https://docs.rs#283)            Some((&mut paragraphs, &mut flags)),
[284](https://docs.rs#284)        );
[285](https://docs.rs#285)
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        InitialInfoExt {
[287](https://docs.rs#287)            base: InitialInfo {
[288](https://docs.rs#288)                text,
[289](https://docs.rs#289)                original_classes,
[290](https://docs.rs#290)                paragraphs,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)            },
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            flags,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)        }
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    }
[295](https://docs.rs#295)}
[296](https://docs.rs#296)
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// Implementation of initial-info computation for both BidiInfo and ParagraphBidiInfo.
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// To treat the text as (potentially) multiple paragraphs, the caller should pass the
[299](https://docs.rs#299)/// pair of optional outparam arrays to receive the ParagraphInfo and pure-ltr flags
[300](https://docs.rs#300)/// for each paragraph. Passing None for split_paragraphs will ignore any paragraph-
[301](https://docs.rs#301)/// separator characters in the text, treating it just as a single paragraph.
[302](https://docs.rs#302)/// Returns the array of BidiClass values for each code unit of the text, along with
[303](https://docs.rs#303)/// the embedding level and pure-ltr flag for the *last* (or only) paragraph.
[304](https://docs.rs#304)fn compute_initial_info<'a, D: BidiDataSource, T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized>(
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    data_source: &D,
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    text: &'a T,
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    default_para_level: Option<Level>,
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    mut split_paragraphs: Option<(&mut Vec<ParagraphInfo>, &mut Vec<ParagraphInfoFlags>)>,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)) -> (Vec<BidiClass>, Level, bool, bool) {
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    let mut original_classes = Vec::with_capacity(text.len());
[311](https://docs.rs#311)
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    // The stack contains the starting code unit index for each nested isolate we're inside.
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    #[cfg(feature = "smallvec")]
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    let mut isolate_stack = SmallVec::<[usize; 8]>::new();
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    #[cfg(not(feature = "smallvec"))]
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    let mut isolate_stack = Vec::new();
[317](https://docs.rs#317)
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    debug_assert!(
[319](https://docs.rs#319)        if let Some((ref paragraphs, ref flags)) = split_paragraphs {
[320](https://docs.rs#320)            paragraphs.is_empty() && flags.is_empty()
[321](https://docs.rs#321)        } else {
[322](https://docs.rs#322)            true
[323](https://docs.rs#323)        }
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    );
[325](https://docs.rs#325)
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    let mut para_start = 0;
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    let mut para_level = default_para_level;
[328](https://docs.rs#328)
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    // Per-paragraph flag: can subsequent processing be skipped? Set to false if any
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    // RTL characters or bidi control characters are encountered in the paragraph.
[331](https://docs.rs#331)    let mut is_pure_ltr = true;
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    // Set to true if any bidi isolation controls are present in the paragraph.
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    let mut has_isolate_controls = false;
[334](https://docs.rs#334)
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    #[cfg(feature = "flame_it")]
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    flame::start("compute_initial_info(): iter text.char_indices()");
[337](https://docs.rs#337)
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    for (i, c) in text.char_indices() {
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        let class = data_source.bidi_class(c);
[340](https://docs.rs#340)
[341](https://docs.rs#341)        #[cfg(feature = "flame_it")]
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        flame::start("original_classes.extend()");
[343](https://docs.rs#343)
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        let len = T::char_len(c);
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        original_classes.extend(repeat(class).take(len));
[346](https://docs.rs#346)
[347](https://docs.rs#347)        #[cfg(feature = "flame_it")]
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        flame::end("original_classes.extend()");
[349](https://docs.rs#349)
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        match class {
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            B => {
[352](https://docs.rs#352)                if let Some((ref mut paragraphs, ref mut flags)) = split_paragraphs {
[353](https://docs.rs#353)                    // P1. Split the text into separate paragraphs. The paragraph separator is kept
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                    // with the previous paragraph.
[355](https://docs.rs#355)                    let para_end = i + len;
[356](https://docs.rs#356)                    paragraphs.push(ParagraphInfo {
[357](https://docs.rs#357)                        range: para_start..para_end,
[358](https://docs.rs#358)                        // P3. If no character is found in p2, set the paragraph level to zero.
[359](https://docs.rs#359)                        level: para_level.unwrap_or(LTR_LEVEL),
[360](https://docs.rs#360)                    });
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                    flags.push(ParagraphInfoFlags {
[362](https://docs.rs#362)                        is_pure_ltr,
[363](https://docs.rs#363)                        has_isolate_controls,
[364](https://docs.rs#364)                    });
[365](https://docs.rs#365)                    // Reset state for the start of the next paragraph.
[366](https://docs.rs#366)                    para_start = para_end;
[367](https://docs.rs#367)                    // TODO: Support defaulting to direction of previous paragraph
[368](https://docs.rs#368)                    //
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                    // <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#HL1>
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                    para_level = default_para_level;
[371](https://docs.rs#371)                    is_pure_ltr = true;
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                    has_isolate_controls = false;
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                    isolate_stack.clear();
[374](https://docs.rs#374)                }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            }
[376](https://docs.rs#376)
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            L | R | AL => {
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                if class != L {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                    is_pure_ltr = false;
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                }
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                match isolate_stack.last() {
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                    Some(&start) => {
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                        if original_classes[start] == FSI {
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                            // X5c. If the first strong character between FSI and its matching
[385](https://docs.rs#385)                            // PDI is R or AL, treat it as RLI. Otherwise, treat it as LRI.
[386](https://docs.rs#386)                            for j in 0..T::char_len(chars::FSI) {
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                                original_classes[start + j] = if class == L { LRI } else { RLI };
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                            }
[389](https://docs.rs#389)                        }
[390](https://docs.rs#390)                    }
[391](https://docs.rs#391)
[392](https://docs.rs#392)                    None => {
[393](https://docs.rs#393)                        if para_level.is_none() {
[394](https://docs.rs#394)                            // P2. Find the first character of type L, AL, or R, while skipping
[395](https://docs.rs#395)                            // any characters between an isolate initiator and its matching
[396](https://docs.rs#396)                            // PDI.
[397](https://docs.rs#397)                            para_level = Some(if class != L { RTL_LEVEL } else { LTR_LEVEL });
[398](https://docs.rs#398)                        }
[399](https://docs.rs#399)                    }
[400](https://docs.rs#400)                }
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            }
[402](https://docs.rs#402)
[403](https://docs.rs#403)            AN | LRE | RLE | LRO | RLO => {
[404](https://docs.rs#404)                is_pure_ltr = false;
[405](https://docs.rs#405)            }
[406](https://docs.rs#406)
[407](https://docs.rs#407)            RLI | LRI | FSI => {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)                is_pure_ltr = false;
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                has_isolate_controls = true;
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                isolate_stack.push(i);
[411](https://docs.rs#411)            }
[412](https://docs.rs#412)
[413](https://docs.rs#413)            PDI => {
[414](https://docs.rs#414)                isolate_stack.pop();
[415](https://docs.rs#415)            }
[416](https://docs.rs#416)
[417](https://docs.rs#417)            _ => {}
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        }
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    }
[420](https://docs.rs#420)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    if let Some((paragraphs, flags)) = split_paragraphs {
[422](https://docs.rs#422)        if para_start < text.len() {
[423](https://docs.rs#423)            paragraphs.push(ParagraphInfo {
[424](https://docs.rs#424)                range: para_start..text.len(),
[425](https://docs.rs#425)                level: para_level.unwrap_or(LTR_LEVEL),
[426](https://docs.rs#426)            });
[427](https://docs.rs#427)            flags.push(ParagraphInfoFlags {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)                is_pure_ltr,
[429](https://docs.rs#429)                has_isolate_controls,
[430](https://docs.rs#430)            });
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        }
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        debug_assert_eq!(paragraphs.len(), flags.len());
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    }
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    debug_assert_eq!(original_classes.len(), text.len());
[435](https://docs.rs#435)
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    #[cfg(feature = "flame_it")]
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    flame::end("compute_initial_info(): iter text.char_indices()");
[438](https://docs.rs#438)
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    (
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        original_classes,
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        para_level.unwrap_or(LTR_LEVEL),
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        is_pure_ltr,
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        has_isolate_controls,
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    )
[445](https://docs.rs#445)}
[446](https://docs.rs#446)
[447](https://docs.rs#447)/// Bidi information of the text.
[448](https://docs.rs#448)///
[449](https://docs.rs#449)/// The `original_classes` and `levels` vectors are indexed by byte offsets into the text.  If a
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// character is multiple bytes wide, then its class and level will appear multiple times in these
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// vectors.
[452](https://docs.rs#452)// TODO: Impl `struct StringProperty<T> { values: Vec<T> }` and use instead of Vec<T>
[453](https://docs.rs#453)#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[454](https://docs.rs#454)pub struct BidiInfo<'text> {
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    /// The text
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    pub text: &'text str,
[457](https://docs.rs#457)
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    /// The BidiClass of the character at each byte in the text.
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    pub original_classes: Vec<BidiClass>,
[460](https://docs.rs#460)
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    /// The directional embedding level of each byte in the text.
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    pub levels: Vec<Level>,
[463](https://docs.rs#463)
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    /// The boundaries and paragraph embedding level of each paragraph within the text.
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    ///
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    /// TODO: Use SmallVec or similar to avoid overhead when there are only one or two paragraphs?
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    /// Or just don't include the first paragraph, which always starts at 0?
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    pub paragraphs: Vec<ParagraphInfo>,
[469](https://docs.rs#469)}
[470](https://docs.rs#470)
[471](https://docs.rs#471)impl<'text> BidiInfo<'text> {
[472](https://docs.rs#472)    /// Split the text into paragraphs and determine the bidi embedding levels for each paragraph.
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    ///
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    ///
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    /// The `hardcoded-data` Cargo feature (enabled by default) must be enabled to use this.
[476](https://docs.rs#476)    ///
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    /// TODO: In early steps, check for special cases that allow later steps to be skipped. like
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    /// text that is entirely LTR.  See the `nsBidi` class from Gecko for comparison.
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    ///
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    /// TODO: Support auto-RTL base direction
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    #[cfg(feature = "hardcoded-data")]
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    #[inline]
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    pub fn new(text: &str, default_para_level: Option<Level>) -> BidiInfo<'_> {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)        Self::new_with_data_source(&HardcodedBidiData, text, default_para_level)
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    }
[487](https://docs.rs#487)
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    /// Split the text into paragraphs and determine the bidi embedding levels for each paragraph, with a custom [`BidiDataSource`]
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    /// for Bidi data. If you just wish to use the hardcoded Bidi data, please use [`BidiInfo::new()`]
[490](https://docs.rs#490)    /// instead (enabled with tbe default `hardcoded-data` Cargo feature).
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    ///
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    /// TODO: In early steps, check for special cases that allow later steps to be skipped. like
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    /// text that is entirely LTR.  See the `nsBidi` class from Gecko for comparison.
[494](https://docs.rs#494)    ///
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    /// TODO: Support auto-RTL base direction
[496](https://docs.rs#496)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    pub fn new_with_data_source<'a, D: BidiDataSource>(
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        data_source: &D,
[499](https://docs.rs#499)        text: &'a str,
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        default_para_level: Option<Level>,
[501](https://docs.rs#501)    ) -> BidiInfo<'a> {
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        let InitialInfoExt { base, flags, .. } =
[503](https://docs.rs#503)            InitialInfoExt::new_with_data_source(data_source, text, default_para_level);
[504](https://docs.rs#504)
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        let mut levels = Vec::<Level>::with_capacity(text.len());
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        let mut processing_classes = base.original_classes.clone();
[507](https://docs.rs#507)
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        for (para, flags) in base.paragraphs.iter().zip(flags.iter()) {
[509](https://docs.rs#509)            let text = &text[para.range.clone()];
[510](https://docs.rs#510)            let original_classes = &base.original_classes[para.range.clone()];
[511](https://docs.rs#511)
[512](https://docs.rs#512)            compute_bidi_info_for_para(
[513](https://docs.rs#513)                data_source,
[514](https://docs.rs#514)                para,
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                flags.is_pure_ltr,
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                flags.has_isolate_controls,
[517](https://docs.rs#517)                text,
[518](https://docs.rs#518)                original_classes,
[519](https://docs.rs#519)                &mut processing_classes,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)                &mut levels,
[521](https://docs.rs#521)            );
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        }
[523](https://docs.rs#523)
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        BidiInfo {
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            text,
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            original_classes: base.original_classes,
[527](https://docs.rs#527)            paragraphs: base.paragraphs,
[528](https://docs.rs#528)            levels,
[529](https://docs.rs#529)        }
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    }
[531](https://docs.rs#531)
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// Produce the levels for this paragraph as needed for reordering, one level per *byte*
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    /// in the paragraph. The returned vector includes bytes that are not included
[534](https://docs.rs#534)    /// in the `line`, but will not adjust them.
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    ///
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    /// This runs [Rule L1], you can run
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    /// [Rule L2] by calling [`Self::reorder_visual()`].
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    /// If doing so, you may prefer to use [`Self::reordered_levels_per_char()`] instead
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    /// to avoid non-byte indices.
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    ///
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// For an all-in-one reordering solution, consider using [`Self::reorder_visual()`].
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    ///
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    /// [Rule L1]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L1
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    /// [Rule L2]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L2
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    pub fn reordered_levels(&self, para: &ParagraphInfo, line: Range<usize>) -> Vec<Level> {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)        assert!(line.start <= self.levels.len());
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        assert!(line.end <= self.levels.len());
[549](https://docs.rs#549)
[550](https://docs.rs#550)        let mut levels = self.levels.clone();
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        let line_classes = &self.original_classes[line.clone()];
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        let line_levels = &mut levels[line.clone()];
[553](https://docs.rs#553)
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        reorder_levels(
[555](https://docs.rs#555)            line_classes,
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            line_levels,
[557](https://docs.rs#557)            self.text.subrange(line),
[558](https://docs.rs#558)            para.level,
[559](https://docs.rs#559)        );
[560](https://docs.rs#560)
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        levels
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    }
[563](https://docs.rs#563)
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    /// Produce the levels for this paragraph as needed for reordering, one level per *character*
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    /// in the paragraph. The returned vector includes characters that are not included
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    /// in the `line`, but will not adjust them.
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    ///
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    /// This runs [Rule L1], you can run
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// [Rule L2] by calling [`Self::reorder_visual()`].
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    /// If doing so, you may prefer to use [`Self::reordered_levels_per_char()`] instead
[571](https://docs.rs#571)    /// to avoid non-byte indices.
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    ///
[573](https://docs.rs#573)    /// For an all-in-one reordering solution, consider using [`Self::reorder_visual()`].
[574](https://docs.rs#574)    ///
[575](https://docs.rs#575)    /// [Rule L1]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L1
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    /// [Rule L2]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L2
[577](https://docs.rs#577)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    pub fn reordered_levels_per_char(
[579](https://docs.rs#579)        &self,
[580](https://docs.rs#580)        para: &ParagraphInfo,
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        line: Range<usize>,
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    ) -> Vec<Level> {
[583](https://docs.rs#583)        let levels = self.reordered_levels(para, line);
[584](https://docs.rs#584)        self.text.char_indices().map(|(i, _)| levels[i]).collect()
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    }
[586](https://docs.rs#586)
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    /// Re-order a line based on resolved levels and return the line in display order.
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    ///
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    /// This does not apply [Rule L3] or [Rule L4] around combining characters or mirroring.
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    ///
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    /// [Rule L3]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L3
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// [Rule L4]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L4
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    pub fn reorder_line(&self, para: &ParagraphInfo, line: Range<usize>) -> Cow<'text, str> {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        if !level::has_rtl(&self.levels[line.clone()]) {
[596](https://docs.rs#596)            return self.text[line].into();
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        }
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        let (levels, runs) = self.visual_runs(para, line.clone());
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        reorder_line(self.text, line, levels, runs)
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    }
[601](https://docs.rs#601)
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    /// Reorders pre-calculated levels of a sequence of characters.
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    ///
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    /// NOTE: This is a convenience method that does not use a `Paragraph`  object. It is
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// intended to be used when an application has determined the levels of the objects (character sequences)
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    /// and just needs to have them reordered.
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    ///
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// the index map will result in `indexMap[visualIndex]==logicalIndex`.
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    ///
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// This only runs [Rule L2](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L2) as it does not have
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    /// information about the actual text.
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    ///
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    /// Furthermore, if `levels` is an array that is aligned with code units, bytes within a codepoint may be
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// reversed. You may need to fix up the map to deal with this. Alternatively, only pass in arrays where each `Level`
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    /// is for a single code point.
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    ///
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    ///
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    ///   # # Example
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    /// ```
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    /// use unicode_bidi::BidiInfo;
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    /// use unicode_bidi::Level;
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    ///
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    /// let l0 = Level::from(0);
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    /// let l1 = Level::from(1);
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// let l2 = Level::from(2);
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    ///
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    /// let levels = vec![l0, l0, l0, l0];
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    /// let index_map = BidiInfo::reorder_visual(&levels);
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// assert_eq!(levels.len(), index_map.len());
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    /// assert_eq!(index_map, [0, 1, 2, 3]);
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    ///
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    /// let levels: Vec<Level> = vec![l0, l0, l0, l1, l1, l1, l2, l2];
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    /// let index_map = BidiInfo::reorder_visual(&levels);
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    /// assert_eq!(levels.len(), index_map.len());
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    /// assert_eq!(index_map, [0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 5, 4, 3]);
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    /// ```
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    #[inline]
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    pub fn reorder_visual(levels: &[Level]) -> Vec<usize> {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        reorder_visual(levels)
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// Find the level runs within a line and return them in visual order.
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    ///
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    /// `line` is a range of bytes indices within `levels`.
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    ///
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    /// The first return value is a vector of levels used by the reordering algorithm,
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    /// i.e. the result of [Rule L1]. The second return value is a vector of level runs,
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    /// the result of [Rule L2], showing the visual order that each level run (a run of text with the
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    /// same level) should be displayed. Within each run, the display order can be checked
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    /// against the Level vector.
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    ///
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    /// This does not handle [Rule L3] (combining characters) or [Rule L4] (mirroring),
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    /// as that should be handled by the engine using this API.
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    ///
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    /// Conceptually, this is the same as running [`Self::reordered_levels()`] followed by
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    /// [`Self::reorder_visual()`], however it returns the result as a list of level runs instead
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    /// of producing a level map, since one may wish to deal with the fact that this is operating on
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    /// byte rather than character indices.
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    /// <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#Reordering_Resolved_Levels>
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    ///
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    /// [Rule L1]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L1
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    /// [Rule L2]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L2
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    /// [Rule L3]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L3
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    /// [Rule L4]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L4
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    #[inline]
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    pub fn visual_runs(
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        &self,
[671](https://docs.rs#671)        para: &ParagraphInfo,
[672](https://docs.rs#672)        line: Range<usize>,
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    ) -> (Vec<Level>, Vec<LevelRun>) {
[674](https://docs.rs#674)        let levels = self.reordered_levels(para, line.clone());
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        visual_runs_for_line(levels, &line)
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    }

[686](https://docs.rs#686)
[687](https://docs.rs#687)/// Bidi information of text treated as a single paragraph.
[688](https://docs.rs#688)///
[689](https://docs.rs#689)/// The `original_classes` and `levels` vectors are indexed by byte offsets into the text.  If a
[690](https://docs.rs#690)/// character is multiple bytes wide, then its class and level will appear multiple times in these
[691](https://docs.rs#691)/// vectors.
[692](https://docs.rs#692)#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[693](https://docs.rs#693)pub struct ParagraphBidiInfo<'text> {
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// The text
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    pub text: &'text str,
[696](https://docs.rs#696)
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    /// The BidiClass of the character at each byte in the text.
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    pub original_classes: Vec<BidiClass>,
[699](https://docs.rs#699)
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    /// The directional embedding level of each byte in the text.
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    pub levels: Vec<Level>,
[702](https://docs.rs#702)
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    /// The paragraph embedding level.
[704](https://docs.rs#704)    pub paragraph_level: Level,
[705](https://docs.rs#705)
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    /// Whether the paragraph is purely LTR.
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    pub is_pure_ltr: bool,
[708](https://docs.rs#708)}
[709](https://docs.rs#709)

[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// Determine the bidi embedding level.

[713](https://docs.rs#713)    ///
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// The `hardcoded-data` Cargo feature (enabled by default) must be enabled to use this.
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    ///
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// TODO: In early steps, check for special cases that allow later steps to be skipped. like

[718](https://docs.rs#718)    ///

[721](https://docs.rs#721)    #[cfg(feature = "hardcoded-data")]

[727](https://docs.rs#727)    /// Determine the bidi embedding level, with a custom [`BidiDataSource`]

[730](https://docs.rs#730)    ///

[734](https://docs.rs#734)    pub fn new_with_data_source<'a, D: BidiDataSource>(

[739](https://docs.rs#739)        // Here we could create a ParagraphInitialInfo struct to parallel the one

[742](https://docs.rs#742)            compute_initial_info(data_source, text, default_para_level, None);
[743](https://docs.rs#743)
[744](https://docs.rs#744)        let mut levels = Vec::<Level>::with_capacity(text.len());
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        let mut processing_classes = original_classes.clone();
[746](https://docs.rs#746)

[748](https://docs.rs#748)            range: Range {
[749](https://docs.rs#749)                start: 0,
[750](https://docs.rs#750)                end: text.len(),
[751](https://docs.rs#751)            },
[752](https://docs.rs#752)            level: paragraph_level,
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        };
[754](https://docs.rs#754)
[755](https://docs.rs#755)        compute_bidi_info_for_para(
[756](https://docs.rs#756)            data_source,
[757](https://docs.rs#757)            ¶_info,
[758](https://docs.rs#758)            is_pure_ltr,

[760](https://docs.rs#760)            text,

[762](https://docs.rs#762)            &mut processing_classes,
[763](https://docs.rs#763)            &mut levels,
[764](https://docs.rs#764)        );
[765](https://docs.rs#765)
[766](https://docs.rs#766)        ParagraphBidiInfo {
[767](https://docs.rs#767)            text,
[768](https://docs.rs#768)            original_classes,
[769](https://docs.rs#769)            levels,

[774](https://docs.rs#774)
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    /// Produce the levels for this paragraph as needed for reordering, one level per *byte*
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    /// in the paragraph. The returned vector includes bytes that are not included
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    /// in the `line`, but will not adjust them.
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    ///
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    /// See BidiInfo::reordered_levels for details.
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    ///
[781](https://docs.rs#781)    /// (This should be kept in sync with BidiInfo::reordered_levels.)
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    pub fn reordered_levels(&self, line: Range<usize>) -> Vec<Level> {
[784](https://docs.rs#784)        assert!(line.start <= self.levels.len());
[785](https://docs.rs#785)        assert!(line.end <= self.levels.len());
[786](https://docs.rs#786)
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        let mut levels = self.levels.clone();
[788](https://docs.rs#788)        let line_classes = &self.original_classes[line.clone()];
[789](https://docs.rs#789)        let line_levels = &mut levels[line.clone()];
[790](https://docs.rs#790)
[791](https://docs.rs#791)        reorder_levels(
[792](https://docs.rs#792)            line_classes,
[793](https://docs.rs#793)            line_levels,
[794](https://docs.rs#794)            self.text.subrange(line),
[795](https://docs.rs#795)            self.paragraph_level,
[796](https://docs.rs#796)        );
[797](https://docs.rs#797)
[798](https://docs.rs#798)        levels
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    }

[810](https://docs.rs#810)        let levels = self.reordered_levels(line);
[811](https://docs.rs#811)        self.text.char_indices().map(|(i, _)| levels[i]).collect()
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    }
[813](https://docs.rs#813)
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    /// Re-order a line based on resolved levels and return the line in display order.
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    ///
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    /// See BidiInfo::reorder_line for details.
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    ///
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    /// (This should be kept in sync with BidiInfo::reorder_line.)
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    pub fn reorder_line(&self, line: Range<usize>) -> Cow<'text, str> {
[821](https://docs.rs#821)        if !level::has_rtl(&self.levels[line.clone()]) {
[822](https://docs.rs#822)            return self.text[line].into();
[823](https://docs.rs#823)        }
[824](https://docs.rs#824)
[825](https://docs.rs#825)        let (levels, runs) = self.visual_runs(line.clone());
[826](https://docs.rs#826)
[827](https://docs.rs#827)        reorder_line(self.text, line, levels, runs)
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    }

[866](https://docs.rs#866)}
[867](https://docs.rs#867)
[868](https://docs.rs#868)/// Return a line of the text in display order based on resolved levels.
[869](https://docs.rs#869)///
[870](https://docs.rs#870)/// `text`   the full text passed to the `BidiInfo` or `ParagraphBidiInfo` for analysis
[871](https://docs.rs#871)/// `line`   a range of byte indices within `text` corresponding to one line
[872](https://docs.rs#872)/// `levels` array of `Level` values, with `line`'s levels reordered into visual order
[873](https://docs.rs#873)/// `runs`   array of `LevelRun`s in visual order
[874](https://docs.rs#874)///
[875](https://docs.rs#875)/// (`levels` and `runs` are the result of calling `BidiInfo::visual_runs()` or
[876](https://docs.rs#876)/// `ParagraphBidiInfo::visual_runs()` for the line of interest.)
[877](https://docs.rs#877)///
[878](https://docs.rs#878)/// Returns: the reordered text of the line.
[879](https://docs.rs#879)///
[880](https://docs.rs#880)/// This does not apply [Rule L3] or [Rule L4] around combining characters or mirroring.
[881](https://docs.rs#881)///
[882](https://docs.rs#882)/// [Rule L3]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L3
[883](https://docs.rs#883)/// [Rule L4]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L4
[884](https://docs.rs#884)fn reorder_line(
[885](https://docs.rs#885)    text: &str,
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    line: Range<usize>,
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    levels: Vec<Level>,
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    runs: Vec<LevelRun>,
[889](https://docs.rs#889)) -> Cow<'_, str> {
[890](https://docs.rs#890)    // If all isolating run sequences are LTR, no reordering is needed
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    if runs.iter().all(|run| levels[run.start].is_ltr()) {
[892](https://docs.rs#892)        return text[line].into();
[893](https://docs.rs#893)    }
[894](https://docs.rs#894)
[895](https://docs.rs#895)    let mut result = String::with_capacity(line.len());
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    for run in runs {
[897](https://docs.rs#897)        if levels[run.start].is_rtl() {
[898](https://docs.rs#898)            result.extend(text[run].chars().rev());
[899](https://docs.rs#899)        } else {
[900](https://docs.rs#900)            result.push_str(&text[run]);
[901](https://docs.rs#901)        }
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    }
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    result.into()
[904](https://docs.rs#904)}
[905](https://docs.rs#905)
[906](https://docs.rs#906)/// Find the level runs within a line and return them in visual order.
[907](https://docs.rs#907)///
[908](https://docs.rs#908)/// `line` is a range of code-unit indices within `levels`.
[909](https://docs.rs#909)///
[910](https://docs.rs#910)/// The first return value is a vector of levels used by the reordering algorithm,
[911](https://docs.rs#911)/// i.e. the result of [Rule L1]. The second return value is a vector of level runs,
[912](https://docs.rs#912)/// the result of [Rule L2], showing the visual order that each level run (a run of text with the
[913](https://docs.rs#913)/// same level) should be displayed. Within each run, the display order can be checked
[914](https://docs.rs#914)/// against the Level vector.
[915](https://docs.rs#915)///
[916](https://docs.rs#916)/// This does not handle [Rule L3] (combining characters) or [Rule L4] (mirroring),
[917](https://docs.rs#917)/// as that should be handled by the engine using this API.
[918](https://docs.rs#918)///
[919](https://docs.rs#919)/// Conceptually, this is the same as running [`reordered_levels()`] followed by
[920](https://docs.rs#920)/// [`reorder_visual()`], however it returns the result as a list of level runs instead
[921](https://docs.rs#921)/// of producing a level map, since one may wish to deal with the fact that this is operating on
[922](https://docs.rs#922)/// byte rather than character indices.
[923](https://docs.rs#923)///
[924](https://docs.rs#924)/// <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#Reordering_Resolved_Levels>
[925](https://docs.rs#925)///
[926](https://docs.rs#926)/// [Rule L1]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L1
[927](https://docs.rs#927)/// [Rule L2]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L2
[928](https://docs.rs#928)/// [Rule L3]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L3
[929](https://docs.rs#929)/// [Rule L4]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L4
[930](https://docs.rs#930)fn visual_runs_for_line(levels: Vec<Level>, line: &Range<usize>) -> (Vec<Level>, Vec<LevelRun>) {
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    // Find consecutive level runs.
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    let mut runs = Vec::new();
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    let mut start = line.start;
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    let mut run_level = levels[start];
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    let mut min_level = run_level;
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    let mut max_level = run_level;
[937](https://docs.rs#937)
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    for (i, &new_level) in levels.iter().enumerate().take(line.end).skip(start + 1) {
[939](https://docs.rs#939)        if new_level != run_level {
[940](https://docs.rs#940)            // End of the previous run, start of a new one.
[941](https://docs.rs#941)            runs.push(start..i);
[942](https://docs.rs#942)            start = i;
[943](https://docs.rs#943)            run_level = new_level;
[944](https://docs.rs#944)            min_level = cmp::min(run_level, min_level);
[945](https://docs.rs#945)            max_level = cmp::max(run_level, max_level);
[946](https://docs.rs#946)        }
[947](https://docs.rs#947)    }
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    runs.push(start..line.end);
[949](https://docs.rs#949)
[950](https://docs.rs#950)    let run_count = runs.len();
[951](https://docs.rs#951)
[952](https://docs.rs#952)    // Re-order the odd runs.
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    // <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L2>
[954](https://docs.rs#954)
[955](https://docs.rs#955)    // Stop at the lowest *odd* level.
[956](https://docs.rs#956)    min_level = min_level.new_lowest_ge_rtl().expect("Level error");
[957](https://docs.rs#957)    // This loop goes through contiguous chunks of level runs that have a level
[958](https://docs.rs#958)    // ≥ max_level and reverses their contents, reducing max_level by 1 each time.
[959](https://docs.rs#959)    while max_level >= min_level {
[960](https://docs.rs#960)        // Look for the start of a sequence of consecutive runs of max_level or higher.
[961](https://docs.rs#961)        let mut seq_start = 0;
[962](https://docs.rs#962)        while seq_start < run_count {
[963](https://docs.rs#963)            if levels[runs[seq_start].start] < max_level {
[964](https://docs.rs#964)                seq_start += 1;
[965](https://docs.rs#965)                continue;
[966](https://docs.rs#966)            }
[967](https://docs.rs#967)
[968](https://docs.rs#968)            // Found the start of a sequence. Now find the end.
[969](https://docs.rs#969)            let mut seq_end = seq_start + 1;
[970](https://docs.rs#970)            while seq_end < run_count {
[971](https://docs.rs#971)                if levels[runs[seq_end].start] < max_level {
[972](https://docs.rs#972)                    break;
[973](https://docs.rs#973)                }
[974](https://docs.rs#974)                seq_end += 1;
[975](https://docs.rs#975)            }
[976](https://docs.rs#976)            // Reverse the runs within this sequence.
[977](https://docs.rs#977)            runs[seq_start..seq_end].reverse();
[978](https://docs.rs#978)
[979](https://docs.rs#979)            seq_start = seq_end;
[980](https://docs.rs#980)        }
[981](https://docs.rs#981)        max_level
[982](https://docs.rs#982)            .lower(1)
[983](https://docs.rs#983)            .expect("Lowering embedding level below zero");
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    }
[985](https://docs.rs#985)    (levels, runs)
[986](https://docs.rs#986)}
[987](https://docs.rs#987)
[988](https://docs.rs#988)/// Reorders pre-calculated levels of a sequence of characters.
[989](https://docs.rs#989)///
[990](https://docs.rs#990)/// NOTE: This is a convenience method that does not use a `Paragraph`  object. It is
[991](https://docs.rs#991)/// intended to be used when an application has determined the levels of the objects (character sequences)
[992](https://docs.rs#992)/// and just needs to have them reordered.
[993](https://docs.rs#993)///
[994](https://docs.rs#994)/// the index map will result in `indexMap[visualIndex]==logicalIndex`.
[995](https://docs.rs#995)///
[996](https://docs.rs#996)/// This only runs [Rule L2](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L2) as it does not have
[997](https://docs.rs#997)/// information about the actual text.
[998](https://docs.rs#998)///
[999](https://docs.rs#999)/// Furthermore, if `levels` is an array that is aligned with code units, bytes within a codepoint may be
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)/// reversed. You may need to fix up the map to deal with this. Alternatively, only pass in arrays where each `Level`
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)/// is for a single code point.
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)fn reorder_visual(levels: &[Level]) -> Vec<usize> {
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)    // Gets the next range of characters after start_index with a level greater
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)    // than or equal to `max`
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)    fn next_range(levels: &[level::Level], mut start_index: usize, max: Level) -> Range<usize> {
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)        if levels.is_empty() || start_index >= levels.len() {
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)            return start_index..start_index;
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)        }
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)        while let Some(l) = levels.get(start_index) {
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)            if *l >= max {
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)                break;
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)            }
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)            start_index += 1;
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)        }
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)        if levels.get(start_index).is_none() {
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)            // If at the end of the array, adding one will
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)            // produce an out-of-range end element
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)            return start_index..start_index;
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)        }
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)        let mut end_index = start_index + 1;
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)        while let Some(l) = levels.get(end_index) {
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)            if *l < max {
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)                return start_index..end_index;
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)            }
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)            end_index += 1;
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)        }
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        start_index..end_index
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)    }
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)    // This implementation is similar to the L2 implementation in `visual_runs()`
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)    // but it cannot benefit from a precalculated LevelRun vector so needs to be different.
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)    if levels.is_empty() {
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)        return vec![];
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)    }
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)    // Get the min and max levels
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)    let (mut min, mut max) = levels
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)        .iter()
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)        .fold((levels[0], levels[0]), |(min, max), &l| {
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)            (cmp::min(min, l), cmp::max(max, l))
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)        });
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)    // Initialize an index map
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)    let mut result: Vec<usize> = (0..levels.len()).collect();
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)    if min == max && min.is_ltr() {
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)        // Everything is LTR and at the same level, do nothing
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)        return result;
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)    }
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)    // Stop at the lowest *odd* level, since everything below that
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)    // is LTR and does not need further reordering
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    min = min.new_lowest_ge_rtl().expect("Level error");
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)    // For each max level, take all contiguous chunks of
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)    // levels ≥ max and reverse them
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)    //
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)    // We can do this check with the original levels instead of checking reorderings because all
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)    // prior reorderings will have been for contiguous chunks of levels >> max, which will
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)    // be a subset of these chunks anyway.
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)    while min <= max {
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)        let mut range = 0..0;
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)        loop {
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)            range = next_range(levels, range.end, max);
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)            result[range.clone()].reverse();
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)            if range.end >= levels.len() {
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)                break;
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)            }
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)        }
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)        max.lower(1).expect("Level error");
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)    }
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)    result
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)}
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)/// The core of BidiInfo initialization, factored out into a function that both
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)/// the utf-8 and utf-16 versions of BidiInfo can use.
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)fn compute_bidi_info_for_para<'a, D: BidiDataSource, T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized>(
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)    data_source: &D,
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)    para: &ParagraphInfo,
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)    is_pure_ltr: bool,
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)    has_isolate_controls: bool,
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)    text: &'a T,
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)    original_classes: &[BidiClass],
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)    processing_classes: &mut [BidiClass],
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)    levels: &mut Vec<Level>,
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)) {
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)    let new_len = levels.len() + para.range.len();
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)    levels.resize(new_len, para.level);
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)    if para.level == LTR_LEVEL && is_pure_ltr {
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)        return;
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)    }
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)    let processing_classes = &mut processing_classes[para.range.clone()];
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)    let levels = &mut levels[para.range.clone()];
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)    let mut level_runs = LevelRunVec::new();
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)    explicit::compute(
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)        text,
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)        para.level,
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)        original_classes,
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)        levels,
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)        processing_classes,
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)        &mut level_runs,
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)    );
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)    let mut sequences = prepare::IsolatingRunSequenceVec::new();
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)    prepare::isolating_run_sequences(
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)        para.level,
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)        original_classes,
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)        levels,
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)        level_runs,
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)        has_isolate_controls,
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)        &mut sequences,
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)    );
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)    for sequence in &sequences {
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)        implicit::resolve_weak(text, sequence, processing_classes);
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)        implicit::resolve_neutral(
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)            text,
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)            data_source,

[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)            original_classes,
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)            processing_classes,
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)        );
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)    }

[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)

[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)/// Produce the levels for this paragraph as needed for reordering, one level per *code unit*
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)/// in the paragraph. The returned vector includes code units that are not included
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)/// in the `line`, but will not adjust them.
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)///
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)/// This runs [Rule L1]
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)///
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)/// [Rule L1]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L1
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)fn reorder_levels<'a, T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized>(
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)    line_classes: &[BidiClass],
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)    line_levels: &mut [Level],
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)    line_text: &'a T,
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)    para_level: Level,
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)) {
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)    // Reset some whitespace chars to paragraph level.
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)    // <http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#L1>
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)    let mut reset_from: Option<usize> = Some(0);
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)    let mut reset_to: Option<usize> = None;
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)    let mut prev_level = para_level;
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)    for ((i, c), (_, length)) in line_text.char_indices().zip(line_text.indices_lengths()) {
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)        match line_classes[i] {
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)            // Segment separator, Paragraph separator
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)            B | S => {
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)                assert_eq!(reset_to, None);
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)                reset_to = Some(i + T::char_len(c));
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)                if reset_from.is_none() {
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)                    reset_from = Some(i);
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)                }
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)            }
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)            // Whitespace, isolate formatting
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)            WS | FSI | LRI | RLI | PDI => {
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)                if reset_from.is_none() {
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)                    reset_from = Some(i);
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)                }
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)            }
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)            // <https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/#Retaining_Explicit_Formatting_Characters>
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)            // same as above + set the level
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)            RLE | LRE | RLO | LRO | PDF | BN => {
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)                if reset_from.is_none() {
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)                    reset_from = Some(i);
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)                }
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)                // also set the level to previous
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)                for level in &mut line_levels[i..i + length] {
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)                    *level = prev_level;
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)                }
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)            }
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)            _ => {
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)                reset_from = None;
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)            }
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)        }
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)        if let (Some(from), Some(to)) = (reset_from, reset_to) {
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)            for level in &mut line_levels[from..to] {
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)                *level = para_level;
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)            }
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)            reset_from = None;
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)            reset_to = None;
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)        }
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)        prev_level = line_levels[i];
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)    }
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)    if let Some(from) = reset_from {
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)        for level in &mut line_levels[from..] {
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)            *level = para_level;
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)        }
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)    }
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)}
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)

[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)/// Return the directionality of the paragraph (Left, Right or Mixed) from its levels.
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)#[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)fn para_direction(levels: &[Level]) -> Direction {
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)    let mut ltr = false;
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)    let mut rtl = false;
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)    for level in levels {
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)        if level.is_ltr() {
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)            ltr = true;
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)            if rtl {
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)                return Direction::Mixed;
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)            }
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)        }
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)        if level.is_rtl() {
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)            rtl = true;
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)            if ltr {
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)                return Direction::Mixed;
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)            }
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)        }
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    }
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    if ltr {
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)        return Direction::Ltr;
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)    }
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)    Direction::Rtl
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)}
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)/// Assign levels to characters removed by rule X9.
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)///
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)/// The levels assigned to these characters are not specified by the algorithm.  This function
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)/// assigns each one the level of the previous character, to avoid breaking level runs.
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)#[cfg_attr(feature = "flame_it", flamer::flame)]
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)fn assign_levels_to_removed_chars(para_level: Level, classes: &[BidiClass], levels: &mut [Level]) {
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    for i in 0..levels.len() {
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)        if prepare::removed_by_x9(classes[i]) {
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)            levels[i] = if i > 0 { levels[i - 1] } else { para_level };
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)        }
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    }
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)}
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)/// Get the base direction of the text provided according to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm.
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)///
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)/// See rules P2 and P3.
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)///
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)/// The base direction is derived from the first character in the string with bidi character type
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)/// L, R, or AL. If the first such character has type L, Direction::Ltr is returned. If the first
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)/// such character has type R or AL, Direction::Rtl is returned.
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)///
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)/// If the string does not contain any character of these types (outside of embedded isolate runs),
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)/// then Direction::Mixed is returned (but should be considered as meaning "neutral" or "unknown",
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)/// not in fact mixed directions).
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)///
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)/// This is a lightweight function for use when only the base direction is needed and no further
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)/// bidi processing of the text is needed.
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)///
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)/// If the text contains paragraph separators, this function considers only the first paragraph.
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)#[cfg(feature = "hardcoded-data")]
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)#[inline]
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)pub fn get_base_direction<'a, T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized>(text: &'a T) -> Direction {
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)    get_base_direction_with_data_source(&HardcodedBidiData, text)
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)}
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)/// Get the base direction of the text provided according to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm,
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)/// considering the full text if the first paragraph is all-neutral.
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)///
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)/// This is the same as get_base_direction except that it does not stop at the first block
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)/// separator, but just resets the embedding level and continues to look for a strongly-
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)/// directional character. So the result will be the base direction of the first paragraph
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)/// that is not purely neutral characters.
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)#[cfg(feature = "hardcoded-data")]
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)#[inline]
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)pub fn get_base_direction_full<'a, T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized>(text: &'a T) -> Direction {
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    get_base_direction_full_with_data_source(&HardcodedBidiData, text)

[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)#[inline]
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)pub fn get_base_direction_with_data_source<'a, D: BidiDataSource, T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized>(

[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)    text: &'a T,

[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)}
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)#[inline]
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)pub fn get_base_direction_full_with_data_source<
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)    'a,
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    D: BidiDataSource,
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)    T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized,
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)>(
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)    data_source: &D,
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)    text: &'a T,
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)) -> Direction {
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)    get_base_direction_impl(data_source, text, true)
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)}
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)fn get_base_direction_impl<'a, D: BidiDataSource, T: TextSource<'a> + ?Sized>(
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)    data_source: &D,
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)    text: &'a T,
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)    use_full_text: bool,
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)) -> Direction {
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)    let mut isolate_level = 0;
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)    for c in text.chars() {
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)        match data_source.bidi_class(c) {
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)            LRI | RLI | FSI => isolate_level += 1,
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)            PDI if isolate_level > 0 => isolate_level -= 1,
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)            L if isolate_level == 0 => return Direction::Ltr,
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)            R | AL if isolate_level == 0 => return Direction::Rtl,
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)            B if !use_full_text => break,
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)            B if use_full_text => isolate_level = 0,
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)            _ => (),
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)        }
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)    }
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)    // If no strong char was found, return Mixed. Normally this will be treated as Ltr by callers
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)    // (see rule P3), but we don't map this to Ltr here so that a caller that wants to apply other
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)    // heuristics to an all-neutral paragraph can tell the difference.
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)    Direction::Mixed
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)}
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)/// Implementation of TextSource for UTF-8 text (a string slice).
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)impl<'text> TextSource<'text> for str {
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)    type CharIter = core::str::Chars<'text>;
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)    type CharIndexIter = core::str::CharIndices<'text>;
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)    type IndexLenIter = Utf8IndexLenIter<'text>;
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)    #[inline]
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)    fn len(&self) -> usize {
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)        (self as &str).len()
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)    }
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)    #[inline]
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)    fn char_at(&self, index: usize) -> Option<(char, usize)> {
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)        if let Some(slice) = self.get(index..) {
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)            if let Some(ch) = slice.chars().next() {
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)                return Some((ch, ch.len_utf8()));
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)            }
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)        }
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)        None
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)    }
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)    #[inline]
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)    fn subrange(&self, range: Range<usize>) -> &Self {
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)        &(self as &str)[range]
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    }
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    #[inline]
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    fn chars(&'text self) -> Self::CharIter {
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)        (self as &str).chars()
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)    }
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)    #[inline]
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)    fn char_indices(&'text self) -> Self::CharIndexIter {
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)        (self as &str).char_indices()
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)    }
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)    #[inline]
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)    fn indices_lengths(&'text self) -> Self::IndexLenIter {
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)        Utf8IndexLenIter::new(self)
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)    }
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)    #[inline]
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)    fn char_len(ch: char) -> usize {
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)        ch.len_utf8()
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)    }
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)}
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)/// Iterator over (UTF-8) string slices returning (index, char_len) tuple.
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)#[derive(Debug)]
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)pub struct Utf8IndexLenIter<'text> {
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    iter: CharIndices<'text>,
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)}
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)impl<'text> Utf8IndexLenIter<'text> {
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)    #[inline]
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)    pub fn new(text: &'text str) -> Self {
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)        Utf8IndexLenIter {
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)            iter: text.char_indices(),
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)        }
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    }
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)}
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)impl Iterator for Utf8IndexLenIter<'_> {
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    type Item = (usize, usize);
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    #[inline]
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)        if let Some((pos, ch)) = self.iter.next() {
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)            return Some((pos, ch.len_utf8()));
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)        }
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)        None
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)    }
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)}
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)#[cfg(test)]
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)fn to_utf16(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)    s.encode_utf16().collect()
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)}

[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)mod tests {

[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)

[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)    #[test]
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)    fn test_utf16_text_source() {
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)        let text: &[u16] =
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)            &[0x41, 0xD801, 0xDC01, 0x20, 0xD800, 0x20, 0xDFFF, 0x20, 0xDC00, 0xD800];
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(0), Some(('A', 1)));
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(1), Some(('\u{10401}', 2)));
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(2), None);
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(3), Some((' ', 1)));
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(4), Some((char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER, 1)));
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(5), Some((' ', 1)));
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(6), Some((char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER, 1)));
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(7), Some((' ', 1)));
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(8), Some((char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER, 1)));
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(9), Some((char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER, 1)));
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)        assert_eq!(text.char_at(10), None);
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)    }

[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)    #[test]
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)    fn test_utf16_char_iter() {
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)        let text: &[u16] =
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)            &[0x41, 0xD801, 0xDC01, 0x20, 0xD800, 0x20, 0xDFFF, 0x20, 0xDC00, 0xD800];
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)        assert_eq!(text.len(), 10);
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)        assert_eq!(text.chars().count(), 9);
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)        let mut chars = text.chars();
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some('A'));
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some('\u{10401}'));
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some(' '));
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some('\u{FFFD}'));
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some(' '));
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some('\u{FFFD}'));
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some(' '));
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some('\u{FFFD}'));
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), Some('\u{FFFD}'));
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)        assert_eq!(chars.next(), None);
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)    }

[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)                BidiInfo {

[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)                    paragraphs: t.4.clone(),
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)                }
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)            );
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)            // If it was empty, also test that ParagraphBidiInfo handles it safely.
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)            if t.4.len() == 0 {
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)                assert_eq!(
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)                    ParagraphBidiInfo::new(t.0, t.1),

[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)                    }
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)                )
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)            }
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)            // If it was a single paragraph, also test ParagraphBidiInfo.
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)            if t.4.len() == 1 {
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)                assert_eq!(
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)                    ParagraphBidiInfo::new(t.0, t.1),
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)                    ParagraphBidiInfo {
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)                        text: t.0,
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)                        original_classes: t.3,

[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)                        paragraph_level: t.4[0].level,
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)                        is_pure_ltr: !level::has_rtl(&t.2),
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)                    }
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)                )
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)            }
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)            let text = &to_utf16(t.0);
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)            assert_eq!(
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)                BidiInfoU16::new(text, t.1),
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)                BidiInfoU16 {
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)                    text,
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)                    levels: t.5.clone(),
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)                    original_classes: t.6.clone(),
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)                    paragraphs: t.7.clone(),
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)                }
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)            );
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)            if t.7.len() == 1 {
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)                assert_eq!(
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)                    ParagraphBidiInfoU16::new(text, t.1),
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)                    ParagraphBidiInfoU16 {
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)                        text: text,
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)                        original_classes: t.6.clone(),
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)                        levels: t.5.clone(),
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)                        paragraph_level: t.7[0].level,

[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)                    }
