# gdscript_scene - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-scene/^0.5.2/

## Expand description

`gdscript-scene` — a `.tscn`/`.tres` **text** parser for scene-aware analysis (Phase 4).

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Godot’s text scene format is INI-like: bracketed section headers (`[node …]`, `[ext_resource …]`,
…) followed by `key = value` property lines. This crate parses that structure — node names,
types, parent paths, attached scripts, `unique_name_in_owner`, and instanced sub-scenes — into a
`SceneModel`**with byte spans**, so the type layer (Phase-4 M1+) can resolve `$Path` /
`%Unique` / `get_node("…")` to a node’s real `Control`/`Node` subclass instead of bare `Node` —
intelligence the Godot editor’s own LSP produces only in-editor and never flows into inference.

**M0 scope:** the pure, wasm-clean [ parse_scene](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scene.html) (

`&str -> SceneModel`) + the model + byte
spans. It **records**the typing inputs (

`type=`/`script=`/`instance=`); it does **not**resolve a

`Ty` (M1), recurse into instanced sub-scenes, build the project-wide script↔scene index, or
cache via salsa (M1+). See `plans/PHASE-4-M0-PLAYBOOK.md`.**Invariant:** the parser is strictly additive and **never fails** — every binary/malformed/
unknown form degrades to an empty-or-partial model + a [ SceneProblem](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneProblem.html), never a panic or

`Err`.
The floor is always parity with the engine’s `Node`-everywhere baseline.**Portability:** a core crate — wasm32-clean (no `std::fs`, no `Instant`, no threads); `.tscn`
text is injected via the VFS exactly like `.gd`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [ExtId](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtId.html)
- An `ext_resource`/`sub_resource`id — the opaque, quoted-string key as written (`"1"`,`"1_app"`,`"StyleBoxFlat_x"`). A 3.x bare-int id is normalized to its string form.
- [ExtResource](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtResource.html)
- An `[ext_resource …]`declaration.
- [NodeIdx](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeIdx.html)
- Index of a node into `SceneModel::nodes`
- [Node](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeProp.html)- Prop
- One body property line of a `[node …]`—`key = value`(value skipped). The key may be a bare identifier (an`@export`var or an engine property) or a`group/sub`override path.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneConnection.html)- Connection
- One `[connection …]`section — a signal wired to a method in the editor. The four spans are the**inner identifier**byte ranges (surrounding quotes excluded), so a rename rewrites exactly the name. A connection has no body.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneModel.html)- Model
- One parsed `.tscn`/`.tres`. Produced by`crate::parse_scene`**never**an`Err`— every malformed/binary/unknown form degrades to an empty-or-partial model plus a`SceneProblem``PartialEq`/`Eq`so it can be a backdated salsa query result (`Arc<SceneModel>`) in M1.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneNode.html)- Node
- One `[node …]`section: its header attributes + the two body properties we read.
- [SubResource](https://docs.rs/struct.SubResource.html)
- A `[sub_resource …]`declaration (type only — the value body is skipped).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Node](https://docs.rs/enum.NodePathResolution.html)- Path - Resolution
- The reason a node path did (not) resolve — for the `INVALID_NODE_PATH`decision (M2).
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneKind.html)- Kind
- Whether the parsed file is a `.tscn`scene (`gd_scene`) or a`.tres`resource (`gd_resource`).
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneProblem.html)- Problem
- A non-fatal problem found during parsing. The parser records these and keeps going — the floor
is always parity with the engine’s `Node`-everywhere baseline.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scene.html)- scene
- Parse `.tscn`/`.tres`text into a`SceneModel``Err`.

# gdscript_syntax - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-syntax/^0.5.2/

## Expand description

`gdscript-syntax` — lexer + indentation pre-pass + lossless parser for GDScript.

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Phase 1 fills this in: a `logos` lexer, a hand-written indentation pre-pass
(INDENT/DEDENT/NEWLINE), and a hand-written recursive-descent parser producing a
lossless [ cstree](https://docs.rs/cstree/0.14.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cstree/index.html) CST plus a typed AST, behind a

`Parser` trait
(tree-sitter-gdscript is the differential test oracle, never the
grammar-of-record — see ADR-0002).The crate “knows nothing about salsa or LSP” (rust-analyzer’s `syntax` layer):
it is pure text → tree. It must build for `wasm32` — no `std::fs`, no clocks, no
threads.

# salsa - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/salsa/=0.27.2/

An integer that uniquely identifies a particular query instance within the
database. Used to track input and output dependencies between queries. Fully
ordered and equatable but those orderings are arbitrary, and meant to be used
only for inserting into maps and the like.

Attach the database to the current thread and execute op.
Allows a different database than currently attached. The original database
will be restored on return.

“Fallback” for maybe-update that is suitable for fully owned T
that implement Eq. In this version, we update only if the new value
is not Eq to the old one. Note that given Eq impls that are not just
structurally comparing fields, this may cause us not to update even if
the value has changed (presumably because this change is not semantically
significant).

---

# text_size - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/text-size/^1.1/

## Expand description

Newtypes for working with text sizes/ranges in a more type-safe manner.

This library can help with two things:

- Reducing storage requirements for offsets and ranges, under the assumption that 32 bits is enough.
- Providing standard vocabulary types for applications where text ranges are pervasive.

However, you should not use this library simply because you work with
strings. In the overwhelming majority of cases, using `usize` and
`std::ops::Range<usize>` is better. In particular, if you are publishing a
library, using only std types in the interface would make it more
interoperable. Similarly, if you are writing something like a lexer, which
produces, but does not *store* text ranges, then sticking to `usize` would
be better.

Minimal Supported Rust Version: latest stable.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextRange.html)- Range
- A range in text, represented as a pair of `TextSize`
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextSize.html)- Size
- A measure of text length. Also, equivalently, an index into text.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [TextLen](https://docs.rs/trait.TextLen.html)
- Primitives with a textual length that can be passed to `TextSize::of`

# criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.8/

## Expand description

A statistics-driven micro-benchmarking library written in Rust.

This crate is a microbenchmarking library which aims to provide strong statistical confidence in detecting and estimating the size of performance improvements and regressions, while also being easy to use.

See
[the user guide](https://criterion-rs.github.io/book/index.html)
for examples as well as details on the measurement and analysis process,
and the output.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features:

- Collects detailed statistics, providing strong confidence that changes to performance are real, not measurement noise.
- Produces detailed charts, providing thorough understanding of your code’s performance behavior.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [async_](https://docs.rs/async_executor/index.html)- executor
- This module defines a trait that can be used to plug in different Futures executors into Criterion.rs’ async benchmarking support.
- [measurement](https://docs.rs/measurement/index.html)
- This module defines a set of traits that can be used to plug different measurements (eg.
Unix’s Processor Time, CPU or GPU performance counters, etc.) into Criterion.rs. It also
includes the `WallTime`
- [profiler](https://docs.rs/profiler/index.html)
- This module provides an extension trait which allows in-process profilers
to be hooked into the `--profile-time`argument at compile-time. Users of out-of-process profilers such as perf don’t need to do anything special.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_group.html)- group
- Macro used to define a function group for the benchmark harness; see the
`criterion_main!`
- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_main.html)- main
- Macro which expands to a benchmark harness.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- Async/await variant of `Bencher`
- [Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html)
- Timer struct used to iterate a benchmarked function and measure the runtime.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkGroup.html)- Group
- Structure used to group together a set of related benchmarks, along with custom configuration settings for groups of benchmarks. All benchmarks performed using a benchmark group will be grouped together in the final report.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkId.html)- Id
- Simple structure representing an ID for a benchmark. The ID must be unique within a benchmark group.
- [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)
- The benchmark manager
- [Plot](https://docs.rs/struct.PlotConfiguration.html)- Configuration
- Contains the configuration options for the plots generated by a particular benchmark or benchmark group.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- Axis scaling type. Specified via `PlotConfiguration::summary_scale`

- Argument to `Bencher::iter_batched``Bencher::iter_batched_ref`
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/enum.BenchmarkFilter.html)- Filter
- Benchmark filtering support.
- [Plotting](https://docs.rs/enum.PlottingBackend.html)- Backend
- Enum used to select the plotting backend.
- [Sampling](https://docs.rs/enum.SamplingMode.html)- Mode
- This enum allows the user to control how Criterion.rs chooses the iteration count when sampling.
The default is `Auto`, which will choose a method automatically based on the iteration time during the warm-up phase.
- [Throughput](https://docs.rs/enum.Throughput.html)
- Enum representing different ways of measuring the throughput of benchmarked code. If the throughput setting is configured for a benchmark then the estimated throughput will be reported as well as the time per iteration.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

# gdscript_ide - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/target-redirect/gdscript_ide/

## Expand description

`gdscript-ide` — the public, engine-/protocol-neutral analysis API.

Modeled on rust-analyzer’s `ide::AnalysisHost` / `ide::Analysis`
(`plans/01-ARCHITECTURE.md` §2). [ AnalysisHost](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html) is the single mutable owner of the
input world;

[is a cheap, cloneable,](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Send` snapshot whose queries take
byte offsets and return plain `serde` result structs from `gdscript-base` — never
`lsp-types`. Each client (LSP server, the guitkx adapter, the CLI, the WASM
playground) maps these POD results to its own protocol.Phase 3 (M0) swaps the engine behind these types from a plain VFS map to a **salsa**
query graph in [ gdscript_db](https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_db/index.html): the input world is now

`FileText` salsa inputs, mutated
through `apply_change`; [is a cloned database handle (salsa handles are](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Clone + Send`, replacing the old `Arc<map>` snapshot). Cancellation is now *real*— a concurrent

`apply_change` cancels in-flight reads on outstanding handles, which unwind
into `Err(Cancelled)` at the query boundary (see [`catch`]). The public API shape is
unchanged. The crate stays `wasm32`-safe (CI guards this).This is the analyzer’s **public Rust API**, so every public item is documented and
`#![deny(missing_docs)]` keeps it that way.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)
- An immutable snapshot of the world — a cloned salsa handle. Every query is `Cancellable``apply_change`cancels in-flight reads, which the client re-issues against the fresh snapshot.
- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html)- Host
- The single mutable owner of analysis state — one per project/workspace.
- [Change](https://docs.rs/struct.Change.html)
- A batch of input changes. `None`text removes the file.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Warning](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html)- Override
- Re-exported so clients can set the warning-strictness override without depending on
`gdscript-db`directly. See`AnalysisHost::set_warning_override``gdscript-hir`/`gdscript-ide`depend on.`#[salsa::db]`on the*trait*makes it a salsa supertrait, so any`&dyn Db`upcasts to`&dyn salsa::Database`and every`#[salsa::tracked]`free function downstream can take`db: &dyn Db`. A host/CLI-level override of the warning-strictness baseline`type_diagnostics`resolves against (regardless of`project.godot`presence). A plain (non-salsa) per-session policy knob: it is read**only**inside the non-tracked`type_diagnostics`, so it never enters the salsa query graph and cannot break the W1 firewall (a warning-level change must never re-run inference).

# gdscript-ide 0.5.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/features

# gdscript-ide

                    There is very little structured metadata to build this page
                    from currently. You should check the

[main library docs](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/gdscript_ide/),[readme](https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-ide/0.5.3), or[Cargo.toml](https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/source/Cargo.toml.orig)in case the author documented the features in them.This release does not have any feature flags.

---

# gdscript_ide - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/gdscript_ide/index.html

## Expand description

`gdscript-ide` — the public, engine-/protocol-neutral analysis API.

Modeled on rust-analyzer’s `ide::AnalysisHost` / `ide::Analysis`
(`plans/01-ARCHITECTURE.md` §2). [ AnalysisHost](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html) is the single mutable owner of the
input world;

[is a cheap, cloneable,](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Send` snapshot whose queries take
byte offsets and return plain `serde` result structs from `gdscript-base` — never
`lsp-types`. Each client (LSP server, the guitkx adapter, the CLI, the WASM
playground) maps these POD results to its own protocol.Phase 3 (M0) swaps the engine behind these types from a plain VFS map to a **salsa**
query graph in [ gdscript_db](https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_db/index.html): the input world is now

`FileText` salsa inputs, mutated
through `apply_change`; [is a cloned database handle (salsa handles are](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Clone + Send`, replacing the old `Arc<map>` snapshot). Cancellation is now *real*— a concurrent

`apply_change` cancels in-flight reads on outstanding handles, which unwind
into `Err(Cancelled)` at the query boundary (see [`catch`]). The public API shape is
unchanged. The crate stays `wasm32`-safe (CI guards this).This is the analyzer’s **public Rust API**, so every public item is documented and
`#![deny(missing_docs)]` keeps it that way.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)
- An immutable snapshot of the world — a cloned salsa handle. Every query is `Cancellable``apply_change`cancels in-flight reads, which the client re-issues against the fresh snapshot.
- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html)- Host
- The single mutable owner of analysis state — one per project/workspace.
- [Change](https://docs.rs/struct.Change.html)
- A batch of input changes. `None`text removes the file.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Warning](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html)- Override
- Re-exported so clients can set the warning-strictness override without depending on
`gdscript-db`directly. See`AnalysisHost::set_warning_override``gdscript-hir`/`gdscript-ide`depend on.`#[salsa::db]`on the*trait*makes it a salsa supertrait, so any`&dyn Db`upcasts to`&dyn salsa::Database`and every`#[salsa::tracked]`free function downstream can take`db: &dyn Db`. A host/CLI-level override of the warning-strictness baseline`type_diagnostics`resolves against (regardless of`project.godot`presence). A plain (non-salsa) per-session policy knob: it is read**only**inside the non-tracked`type_diagnostics`, so it never enters the salsa query graph and cannot break the W1 firewall (a warning-level change must never re-run inference).

---

[87](#87)    }

[98](#98)    }

[114](#114)impl AnalysisHost {
[115](#115)    #[must_use]
[117](#117)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[118](#118)        Self::default()
[119](#119)    }
[120](#120)
[121](#121)    pub fn apply_change(&mut self, change: Change) {
[125](#125)        let mut structure_changed = false;
[126](#126)        for (id, text) in change.files {
[127](#127)            if let Some(t) = text {
[128](#128)                structure_changed |= self.db.file_text(id).is_none();
[130](#130)                self.db.set_file_text(id, &t, Durability::LOW);
[131](#131)            } else {
[132](#132)                structure_changed |= self.db.file_text(id).is_some();
[133](#133)                self.db.remove_file(id);
[134](#134)            }
[135](#135)        }
[136](#136)        for (id, path) in change.paths {
[140](#140)            self.db.set_file_path(id, &path);
[141](#141)        }
[142](#142)        if let Some(text) = change.project_config {
[145](#145)            self.db.set_project_config(&text);
[146](#146)        }
[147](#147)        if structure_changed {
[150](#150)            self.db.sync_source_root();
[151](#151)        }
[152](#152)        if let Some(complete) = change.workspace_complete {
[155](#155)            self.db.set_workspace_complete(complete);
[156](#156)        }
[157](#157)    }
[158](#158)
[159](#159)    pub fn set_engine_api(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
[167](#167)        match gdscript_api::EngineApi::from_bytes(bytes) {
[168](#168)            Ok(api) => {
[169](#169)                self.db.set_engine_api(api);
[170](#170)                true
[171](#171)            }
[172](#172)            Err(_) => false,
[173](#173)        }
[174](#174)    }
[175](#175)
[176](#176)    pub fn set_warning_override(&mut self, ov: gdscript_db::WarningOverride) {
[180](#180)        self.db.set_warning_override(ov);
[181](#181)    }
[182](#182)
[183](#183)    #[must_use]
[185](#185)    pub fn analysis(&self) -> Analysis {
[186](#186)        Analysis {
[187](#187)            db: self.db.clone(),
[188](#188)        }
[189](#189)    }

[201](#201)    pub fn syntax_tree(&self, file: FileId) -> Cancellable<Option<String>> {
[208](#208)        catch(|| {
[209](#209)            self.db
[210](#210)                .file_text(file)
[211](#211)                .map(|ft| gdscript_db::parse(&self.db, ft).debug_tree())
[212](#212)        })
[213](#213)    }
[214](#214)
[215](#215)    pub fn diagnostics(&self, file: FileId) -> Cancellable<Vec<Diagnostic>> {
[220](#220)        catch(|| {
[221](#221)            self.db
[222](#222)                .file_text(file)
[223](#223)                .map(|ft| {
[224](#224)                    let mut diags = features::diagnostics(&self.db, ft);
[225](#225)                    diags.extend(semantic::type_diagnostics(&self.db, ft));
[226](#226)                    diags
[227](#227)                })
[228](#228)                .unwrap_or_default()
[229](#229)        })
[230](#230)    }
[231](#231)
[232](#232)    pub fn format(&self, file: FileId) -> Cancellable<Option<String>> {
[239](#239)        catch(|| {
[240](#240)            self.db.file_text(file).map(|ft| {
[241](#241)                gdscript_fmt::format(ft.text(&self.db), &gdscript_fmt::FmtConfig::default())
[242](#242)            })
[243](#243)        })
[244](#244)    }
[245](#245)
[246](#246)    pub fn format_range(
[253](#253)        &self,
[254](#254)        file: FileId,
[255](#255)        start: u32,
[256](#256)        end: u32,
[257](#257)    ) -> Cancellable<Option<(u32, u32, String)>> {
[258](#258)        catch(|| {
[259](#259)            self.db.file_text(file).and_then(|ft| {
[260](#260)                let sel = (start as usize)..(end as usize);
[261](#261)                gdscript_fmt::format_range(
[262](#262)                    ft.text(&self.db),
[263](#263)                    &gdscript_fmt::FmtConfig::default(),
[264](#264)                    sel,
[265](#265)                )
[266](#266)                .map(|e| {
[267](#267)                    (
[268](#268)                        u32::try_from(e.range.start).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
[269](#269)                        u32::try_from(e.range.end).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
[270](#270)                        e.new_text,
[271](#271)                    )
[272](#272)                })
[273](#273)            })
[274](#274)        })
[275](#275)    }
[276](#276)

[325](#325)        catch(|| {

[328](#328)                .map(|ft| {
[329](#329)                    semantic::node_path_completions(&self.db, ft, pos.offset)
[330](#330)                        .or_else(|| semantic::member_completions(&self.db, ft, pos.offset))

[332](#332)                })
[333](#333)                .unwrap_or_default()
[334](#334)        })

[432](#432)    fn host_with(src: &str) -> (AnalysisHost, FileId) {
[433](#433)        let mut host = AnalysisHost::new();
[434](#434)        let file = FileId(0);
[435](#435)        let mut change = Change::new();
[436](#436)        change.change_file(file, src);
[437](#437)        host.apply_change(change);
[438](#438)        (host, file)
[439](#439)    }

[441](#441)    #[test]
[442](#442)    fn snapshot_reads_applied_files() {
[443](#443)        let (host, file) = host_with("func f():\n\tpass\n");
[444](#444)        let analysis = host.analysis();
[445](#445)        let symbols = analysis.document_symbols(file).unwrap();
[446](#446)        assert_eq!(symbols.len(), 1);
[447](#447)        assert_eq!(symbols[0].name, "f");
[448](#448)    }

[451](#451)    fn preload_resolves_cross_file_through_the_public_api() {
[452](#452)        let mut host = AnalysisHost::new();
[455](#455)        let mut change = Change::new();
[456](#456)        change.change_file(
[457](#457)            FileId(0),
[458](#458)            "class_name Markup\nfunc parse() -> int:\n\treturn 1\n",
[459](#459)        );
[460](#460)        change.set_file_path(FileId(0), "res://markup.gd");
[461](#461)        change.change_file(
[462](#462)            FileId(1),
[463](#463)            "const M = preload(\"res://markup.gd\")\nfunc go():\n\tvar n := M.new().parse()\n\treturn n\n",
[464](#464)        );
[465](#465)        change.set_file_path(FileId(1), "res://main.gd");
[466](#466)        host.apply_change(change);
[467](#467)        let analysis = host.analysis();
[468](#468)
[469](#469)        assert!(analysis.diagnostics(FileId(1)).unwrap().is_empty());
[471](#471)        let hints = analysis.inlay_hints(FileId(1)).unwrap();
[474](#474)        assert!(
[475](#475)            hints.iter().any(|h| h.label.contains("int")),
[476](#476)            "expected an `: int` inlay on the preload-resolved binding, got {hints:?}",
[477](#477)        );
[478](#478)    }

[572](#572)    fn scene_node_path_typing_through_the_public_api() {
[573](#573)        let mut host = AnalysisHost::new();
[576](#576)        let mut change = Change::new();
[577](#577)        change.change_file(
[578](#578)            FileId(0),
[579](#579)            "[gd_scene format=3]\n\
[580](#580)             [ext_resource type=\"Script\" path=\"res://main.gd\" id=\"1\"]\n\
[581](#581)             [node name=\"Root\" type=\"Control\"]\n\
[582](#582)             script = ExtResource(\"1\")\n\
[583](#583)             [node name=\"Btn\" type=\"Button\" parent=\".\"]\n",
[584](#584)        );
[585](#585)        change.set_file_path(FileId(0), "res://main.tscn");
[586](#586)        change.change_file(
[587](#587)            FileId(1),
[588](#588)            "extends Control\nfunc _ready():\n\tvar b := $Btn\n\tb.show()\n",
[589](#589)        );
[590](#590)        change.set_file_path(FileId(1), "res://main.gd");
[591](#591)        host.apply_change(change);
[592](#592)        let analysis = host.analysis();
[593](#593)
[594](#594)        assert!(analysis.diagnostics(FileId(1)).unwrap().is_empty());
[595](#595)        let hints = analysis.inlay_hints(FileId(1)).unwrap();
[596](#596)        assert!(
[597](#597)            hints.iter().any(|h| h.label.contains("Button")),

[797](#797)    fn completion_is_scope_aware_for_locals_and_params() {
[798](#798)        let mut host = AnalysisHost::new();
[803](#803)        let mut change = Change::new();
[804](#804)        let gd = "var member_v := 0\nfunc a(pa):\n\tvar la := 1\n\t\nfunc b(pb):\n\tvar lb := 2\n";
[805](#805)        change.change_file(FileId(0), gd);
[806](#806)        change.set_file_path(FileId(0), "res://m.gd");
[807](#807)        host.apply_change(change);
[808](#808)        let analysis = host.analysis();
[809](#809)
[810](#810)        let upto = "var member_v := 0\nfunc a(pa):\n\tvar la := 1\n\t";
[812](#812)        let offset = u32::try_from(gd.find(upto).unwrap() + upto.len()).unwrap();
[813](#813)        let items = analysis
[814](#814)            .completions(FilePosition {
[815](#815)                file: FileId(0),
[816](#816)                offset,
[817](#817)            })
[818](#818)            .unwrap();
[819](#819)        let labels: Vec<_> = items.iter().map(|i| i.label.as_str()).collect();
[820](#820)        assert!(labels.contains(&"pa"), "own param `pa`: {labels:?}");
[822](#822)        assert!(labels.contains(&"la"), "own local `la`: {labels:?}");
[823](#823)        assert!(labels.contains(&"member_v"), "class member: {labels:?}");
[824](#824)        assert!(
[825](#825)            labels.contains(&"a") && labels.contains(&"b"),
[826](#826)            "sibling func names: {labels:?}",
[827](#827)        );
[828](#828)        assert!(!labels.contains(&"pb"), "leaked b's param: {labels:?}");
[830](#830)        assert!(!labels.contains(&"lb"), "leaked b's local: {labels:?}");
[831](#831)    }

[868](#868)            ("var f := func(px):\n\treturn px\n", "px", "return "),

[871](#871)            ("func foo(ia): return ia\n", "ia", "return "),
[872](#872)        ];
[873](#873)        for (gd, param, marker) in cases {
[874](#874)            let mut host = AnalysisHost::new();

[877](#877)            change.set_file_path(FileId(0), "res://m.gd");

[882](#882)                .completions(FilePosition {
[883](#883)                    file: FileId(0),
[884](#884)                    offset,
[885](#885)                })
[886](#886)                .unwrap()
[887](#887)                .into_iter()
[888](#888)                .map(|i| i.label)
[889](#889)                .collect();
[890](#890)            assert!(
[891](#891)                labels.iter().any(|l| l == param),
[892](#892)                "param `{param}` should be offered inside its body for {gd:?}, got {labels:?}",
[893](#893)            );
[894](#894)        }

[903](#903)        let scene = "[gd_scene format=3]\n\
[904](#904)             [ext_resource type=\"Script\" path=\"res://main.gd\" id=\"1\"]\n\
[905](#905)             [node name=\"Root\" type=\"Control\"]\n\
[906](#906)             script = ExtResource(\"1\")\n\
[907](#907)             [node name=\"Btn\" type=\"Button\" parent=\".\"]\n";
[908](#908)        let gd = "extends Control\nfunc _ready():\n\tvar b := $Btn\n";
[909](#909)        change.change_file(FileId(0), scene);
[910](#910)        change.set_file_path(FileId(0), "res://main.tscn");
[911](#911)        change.change_file(FileId(1), gd);
[912](#912)        change.set_file_path(FileId(1), "res://main.gd");
[913](#913)        host.apply_change(change);
[914](#914)        let analysis = host.analysis();
[915](#915)
[916](#916)        let offset = u32::try_from(gd.find("$Btn").unwrap() + 1).unwrap(); let targets = analysis
[918](#918)            .goto_definition(FilePosition {
[919](#919)                file: FileId(1),
[920](#920)                offset,
[921](#921)            })
[922](#922)            .unwrap();
[923](#923)        assert_eq!(targets.len(), 1, "{targets:?}");
[924](#924)        assert_eq!(targets[0].file, FileId(0), "jumps into the .tscn");
[925](#925)        let focus =
[926](#926)            &scene[targets[0].focus_range.start as usize..targets[0].focus_range.end as usize];
[927](#927)        assert!(
[928](#928)            focus.contains("Btn"),
[929](#929)            "focus on the node name, got {focus:?}"
[930](#930)        );

# AnalysisHost in gdscript_ide - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/gdscript_ide/struct.AnalysisHost.html

`pub struct AnalysisHost { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The single mutable owner of analysis state — one per project/workspace.

The input world is a virtual file system (`FileId` → UTF-8 text) held as salsa inputs; the
host never reads paths. Clients push text via [ AnalysisHost::apply_change](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html#method.apply_change).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#114-190)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AnalysisHost)### impl [AnalysisHost](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#114-190)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AnalysisHost)

### impl [AnalysisHost](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#124-157)#### pub fn [apply_change](https://docs.rs#method.apply_change)(&mut self, change: [Change](https://docs.rs/struct.Change.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#124-157)

#### pub fn [apply_change](https://docs.rs#method.apply_change)(&mut self, change: [Change](https://docs.rs/struct.Change.html))

Apply a batch of input changes. The **only** mutation entry point — each `set`/`remove`
bumps the salsa revision (and cancels any in-flight reads on outstanding [ Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)
handles). Edited files are

`LOW` durability (they change every keystroke).[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#166-174)#### pub fn [set_engine_api](https://docs.rs#method.set_engine_api)(&mut self, bytes: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#166-174)

#### pub fn [set_engine_api](https://docs.rs#method.set_engine_api)(&mut self, bytes: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Install a runtime-fetched engine model — the **wasm path** (an `extension_api` blob the host
`fetch`ed and brotli-decoded, decoded here via `EngineApi::from_bytes`). Native builds use the
bundled model and normally never call this. Returns `false` (rather than panicking) if the
bytes fail to decode, leaving the model unset. First install wins (load-once); installing it
**after** queries have already run correctly recomputes them — the wasm engine-generation
input invalidates the affected reads, so loading the blob async (after opening a document) is
safe, not just loading it first.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#179-181)#### pub fn [set_warning_override](https://docs.rs#method.set_warning_override)(&mut self, ov: [WarningOverride](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_ide/lib.rs.html#179-181)

#### pub fn [set_warning_override](https://docs.rs#method.set_warning_override)(&mut self, ov: [WarningOverride](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html))

Force a warning-strictness baseline regardless of `project.godot` presence (the CLI
`--strict` / `--engine-defaults` knob; an LSP could set it per session). A plain `Db` field,
not a salsa input — changing it never re-runs inference, only the downstream gate.

# Analysis in gdscript_ide - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide/0.5.3/gdscript_ide/struct.Analysis.html

`pub struct Analysis { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Format `file`’s source, returning the tidied text — or `None` if the file is unknown.
Safe by construction: it normalizes whitespace + indentation and never changes meaning,
falling back to the original on anything it can’t safely reformat (see [ gdscript_fmt](https://docs.rs/gdscript-fmt/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_fmt/index.html)).

# gdscript_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_db/index.html

## Expand description

`gdscript-db` — the input layer for the analyzer.

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Holds the virtual file system (`FileId` → text, always injected — never `std::fs`), the
project model, and (from Phase 3) the **salsa** query graph: `#[salsa::input]`s set via
`apply_change`, `#[salsa::tracked]` derived queries, durability tiers. The Phase-0/1/2
plain VFS map + reparse-on-change is being replaced here, localized behind the unchanged
`gdscript-ide` public API (Playbook §3.M0).

Crate boundary: `gdscript-db` is the *base* of the salsa stack — it owns the [ Db](https://docs.rs/trait.Db.html) trait,
the inputs, and the

[query (it may depend on](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)

`parse``gdscript-syntax`, never on
`gdscript-hir`). The higher queries (`item_tree`, `analyze_file`) live in `gdscript-hir`,
which depends on this crate for `&dyn Db`. This one-way layering is what avoids a
`db ↔ hir` dependency cycle.`FileId` is deliberately **not** a salsa input. The `FileId → FileText` mapping is a side
table ([ Files](https://docs.rs/struct.Files.html)) the database owns, mirroring rust-analyzer’s

`base-db`: `FileId`s are
assigned by the client/loader and stay opaque ids, while the salsa input is the *text*.

Must build for `wasm32` (single-threaded; salsa with `default-features = false`).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Engine](https://docs.rs/struct.EngineGeneration.html)- Generation
- A generation counter that makes the otherwise-untracked runtime engine model **invalidate**correctly. The engine model is a leaked`&'static`side handle (not a salsa input), so a query memoized while it was still absent (`engine() == None`, on`wasm32`before`set_engine_api`) would otherwise return that stale empty result forever. Every`engine()`read records a dependency on this input;`set_engine_api`bumps it, recomputing those queries. The*value*is irrelevant — only that setting it advances the revision. Used on`wasm32`only (native has the bundled model from the start, so it never changes — no generation tracking, no overhead).
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileText.html)- Text
- The VFS leaf: one file’s UTF-8 text, as a salsa input, plus its `FileId``FileText`can recover the id for cross-file resolution) and its`res://`path (so`preload`/`extends "res://…"`resolve to the declaring file — M3).
- [Files](https://docs.rs/struct.Files.html)
- The `FileId → FileText`side table.`Arc`-backed so a cheap clone shares the same map — needed to mutate an input (`&mut dyn Db`) without simultaneously borrowing`self.files`.
- [Project](https://docs.rs/struct.ProjectConfig.html)- Config
- The project’s `project.godot`, injected as raw text — the wasm-clean core never reads the filesystem, so the loader pushes the bytes exactly like a`.gd`file. The autoload index is a tracked query that parses this text (M4). Held at`MEDIUM`durability (project structure, stable across`.gd`keystrokes), so a body edit (LOW) never invalidates the autoload registry.
- [Root](https://docs.rs/struct.RootDatabase.html)- Database
- The concrete analyzer database — a salsa `Storage`plus the`Files`
- [Source](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceRoot.html)- Root
- The project’s file set — a salsa input so project-wide queries (the global `class_name`registry, M1) iterate the files incrementally. It changes only when a file is**added or removed**, never on a body edit, and is held at MEDIUM durability — so a keystroke (a`LOW`change) never invalidates project-wide derived data.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Warning](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html)- Override
- The database trait `gdscript-hir`/`gdscript-ide`depend on.`#[salsa::db]`on the*trait*makes it a salsa supertrait, so any`&dyn Db`upcasts to`&dyn salsa::Database`and every`#[salsa::tracked]`free function downstream can take`db: &dyn Db`. A host/CLI-level override of the warning-strictness baseline`type_diagnostics`resolves against (regardless of`project.godot`presence). A plain (non-salsa) per-session policy knob: it is read**only**inside the non-tracked`type_diagnostics`, so it never enters the salsa query graph and cannot break the W1 firewall (a warning-level change must never re-run inference).

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Parse a file to its lossless CST. Memoized; re-parses only when the file text changes.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

`files: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<([FileId](https://docs.rs/gdscript-base/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_base/struct.FileId.html), [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>>)>Files to add/replace (`Some`) or remove (`None`).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.paths)

`paths: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<([FileId](https://docs.rs/gdscript-base/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_base/struct.FileId.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))>Each file’s `res://` path (loader-supplied; M3 `preload`/`extends "res://…"` resolution).
Supply it when a file is **added**; it is stable across edits, so a keystroke change must
omit it (salsa bumps an input field’s revision on *every* set, even an identical value, so
re-sending a path each edit would needlessly invalidate the `res_path_registry`).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.project_config)

`project_config: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>>The project’s `project.godot` text (loader-supplied; M4 `[autoload]` resolution). Set once
on project open / when it changes; omit on `.gd` keystrokes.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.workspace_complete)

`workspace_complete: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>The loader’s claim that the file set is the **whole project** (every `.gd` under the
project root) — the gate for absence-based diagnostics (`UNDEFINED_FUNCTION` /
`UNDEFINED_IDENTIFIER`). Set once at load; omit on edits. `None` leaves it unchanged.

# gdscript-hir 0.5.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-hir/0.5.3

# gdscript-hir

The **semantic layer** — name resolution, gradual type inference, and the GDScript
warning checks. This is where source becomes *understood*: what each identifier
refers to, what type each expression has, and which lints fire.

An internal layer of ** gdscript-analyzer**,
a fast, embeddable GDScript (Godot 4.x) static-analysis library ("Roslyn for
Godot"). You normally don't depend on this crate directly — use

**(the public API), or the**

`gdscript-ide`**(Node) /**

`@gdscript-analyzer/core`**(browser) packages.**

`@gdscript-analyzer/wasm`- **API docs:**- [https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir](https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir)
- **Crate map:**- [repo README](https://github.com/yanivkalfa/gdscript-analyzer#the-workspace--crates--packages)
- **License:**MIT OR Apache-2.0

---

# unicode_security - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicode-security/^0.1/

## Expand description

Detect possible security problems with Unicode usage according to
[Unicode Technical Standard #39](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/)
rules.

```
extern crate unicode_security;
use unicode_security::GeneralSecurityProfile;
fn main() {
    let ch = 'µ'; // U+00B5 MICRO SIGN
    let allowed = 'µ'.identifier_allowed();
    println!("{}", ch);
    println!("The above char is {} in unicode identifiers.",
             if allowed { "allowed" } else { "restricted" });
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)features

unicode-security supports a `no_std` feature. This eliminates dependence
on std, and instead uses equivalent functions from core.

[§](https://docs.rs#cratesio)crates.io

You can use this package in your project by adding the following
to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
unicode-security = "0.0.1"
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use confusable_detection::`- [skeleton](https://docs.rs/confusable_detection/fn.skeleton.html);
- `pub use general_security_profile::`- [GeneralSecurityProfile](https://docs.rs/general_security_profile/trait.GeneralSecurityProfile.html);
- `pub use mixed_script::`- [is_potential_mixed_script_confusable_char](https://docs.rs/mixed_script/fn.is_potential_mixed_script_confusable_char.html);
- `pub use mixed_script::`- [MixedScript](https://docs.rs/mixed_script/trait.MixedScript.html);
- `pub use restriction_level::`- [RestrictionLevel](https://docs.rs/restriction_level/enum.RestrictionLevel.html);
- `pub use restriction_level::`- [RestrictionLevelDetection](https://docs.rs/restriction_level/trait.RestrictionLevelDetection.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [confusable_](https://docs.rs/confusable_detection/index.html)- detection
- [Confusable detection](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#Confusable_Detection)
- [general_](https://docs.rs/general_security_profile/index.html)- security_ - profile
- Utilities for working with the [General Security Profile](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#General_Security_Profile)for identifiers
- [mixed_](https://docs.rs/mixed_script/index.html)- script
- [Mixed-script detection](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#Mixed_Script_Detection)
- [restriction_](https://docs.rs/restriction_level/index.html)- level
- For detecting the [restriction level](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#Restriction_Level_Detection)a string conforms to

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [UNICODE_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNICODE_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- The version of [Unicode](http://www.unicode.org/)that this version of unicode-security is based on.

# gdscript_hir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/index.html

## Expand description

`gdscript-hir` — the semantic / type layer.

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Lowers the AST to a HIR (an `ItemTree` of signatures + per-function `Body`), runs name resolution
(local → class member → inherited → global), gradual type inference (Variant by default,
`:=`/annotations, member lookup over the engine inheritance table, `is`/`as` narrowing), and the
GDScript warning checks. Single-file in Phase 2; project-wide + scene-aware later.

Phase 2 builds this out bottom-up: the type model ([ ty](https://docs.rs/ty/index.html)), then the item tree, body, name
resolution, and inference. Must build for

`wasm32`.## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [body](https://docs.rs/body/index.html)
- Body lowering (Playbook §3.1/§3.4): a function body (or a class-level initializer
expression) lowered from the CST into a flat arena of `Expr``Stmt``ExprId``StmtId``BodySourceMap``ExprId``ExprId`through this source map, then reads the inferred type from`crate::infer`
- [def](https://docs.rs/def/index.html)
- Canonical symbol identity + cursor classification (Playbook §3.M5) — the basis of cross-file navigation (find-references, rename, goto-definition).
- [flow](https://docs.rs/flow/index.html)
- Per-body control-flow narrowing (Phase-6 Workstream 2).
- [infer](https://docs.rs/infer/index.html)
- Gradual type inference (Playbook §3.3–§3.6 + §5): a single forward, bottom-up,
bidirectional walk over a lowered `Body`*structure*, Pyright’s gradual*semantics*).
- [item_](https://docs.rs/item_tree/index.html)- tree
- The item tree (Playbook §3.1): a signature-level view of one `.gd`file — its`class_name`,`extends`target, and class members (funcs/vars/consts/signals/enums/inner classes) — lowered from the CST**without reading any function body**.
- [project](https://docs.rs/project/index.html)
- `project.godot`autoload parsing (Playbook §3.M4).
- [queries](https://docs.rs/queries/index.html)
- The salsa-tracked entry points for the semantic layer, layered on `gdscript-db`’s`parse`
- [resolve](https://docs.rs/resolve/index.html)
- Name & type resolution (Playbook §3.2/§3.5): the `resolve_external``Ty``ClassScope`
- [ty](https://docs.rs/ty/index.html)
- The Phase-2 type model (Playbook §2/§3.5): the gradual `Ty``Variant`, the hard/soft`TypeSource``is_assignable`compatibility check, and`TyRef`→`Ty`resolution against the engine API.
- [warnings](https://docs.rs/warnings/index.html)
- The Godot warning catalog + the emit-then-gate seam (Phase-6 Workstream 1).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AstPtr](https://docs.rs/struct.AstPtr.html)
- A reparse-stable pointer to a syntax node — its `SyntaxKind``TextRange``SyntaxNodePtr`). Because it is plain`Copy`data keyed on text position, identical source re-parses to the identical pointer, which is what lets the`crate::item_tree::ItemTree``Eq`while still being able to recover the CST node for deferred body lowering / initializer inference.

---

# gdscript_ide - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide

## Expand description

`gdscript-ide` — the public, engine-/protocol-neutral analysis API.

Modeled on rust-analyzer’s `ide::AnalysisHost` / `ide::Analysis`
(`plans/01-ARCHITECTURE.md` §2). [ AnalysisHost](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html) is the single mutable owner of the
input world;

[is a cheap, cloneable,](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Send` snapshot whose queries take
byte offsets and return plain `serde` result structs from `gdscript-base` — never
`lsp-types`. Each client (LSP server, the guitkx adapter, the CLI, the WASM
playground) maps these POD results to its own protocol.Phase 3 (M0) swaps the engine behind these types from a plain VFS map to a **salsa**
query graph in [ gdscript_db](https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_db/index.html): the input world is now

`FileText` salsa inputs, mutated
through `apply_change`; [is a cloned database handle (salsa handles are](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)

`Analysis``Clone + Send`, replacing the old `Arc<map>` snapshot). Cancellation is now *real*— a concurrent

`apply_change` cancels in-flight reads on outstanding handles, which unwind
into `Err(Cancelled)` at the query boundary (see [`catch`]). The public API shape is
unchanged. The crate stays `wasm32`-safe (CI guards this).This is the analyzer’s **public Rust API**, so every public item is documented and
`#![deny(missing_docs)]` keeps it that way.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.Analysis.html)
- An immutable snapshot of the world — a cloned salsa handle. Every query is `Cancellable``apply_change`cancels in-flight reads, which the client re-issues against the fresh snapshot.
- [Analysis](https://docs.rs/struct.AnalysisHost.html)- Host
- The single mutable owner of analysis state — one per project/workspace.
- [Change](https://docs.rs/struct.Change.html)
- A batch of input changes. `None`text removes the file.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Warning](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html)- Override
- Re-exported so clients can set the warning-strictness override without depending on
`gdscript-db`directly. See`AnalysisHost::set_warning_override``gdscript-hir`/`gdscript-ide`depend on.`#[salsa::db]`on the*trait*makes it a salsa supertrait, so any`&dyn Db`upcasts to`&dyn salsa::Database`and every`#[salsa::tracked]`free function downstream can take`db: &dyn Db`. A host/CLI-level override of the warning-strictness baseline`type_diagnostics`resolves against (regardless of`project.godot`presence). A plain (non-salsa) per-session policy knob: it is read**only**inside the non-tracked`type_diagnostics`, so it never enters the salsa query graph and cannot break the W1 firewall (a warning-level change must never re-run inference).

---

# gdscript_hir::ty - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/ty/index.html

## Expand description

The Phase-2 type model (Playbook §2/§3.5): the gradual [ Ty](https://docs.rs/enum.Ty.html) lattice over

`Variant`, the
hard/soft [, the ported](https://docs.rs/enum.TypeSource.html)

`TypeSource``is_assignable` compatibility check, and `TyRef`→`Ty`
resolution against the engine API.GDScript is gradually typed over one runtime value type, `Variant`. Three top-ish types are
kept distinct on purpose: [ Ty::Variant](https://docs.rs/enum.Ty.html#variant.Variant) (the absorbing gradual top),

[(the Phase-3 cross-file seam — never warns, never cascades, elided from hover), and](https://docs.rs/enum.Ty.html#variant.Unknown)

`Ty::Unknown`[(already diagnosed — suppresses further cascade).](https://docs.rs/enum.Ty.html#variant.Error)

`Ty::Error`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [EnumRef](https://docs.rs/struct.EnumRef.html)
- A reference to an enum type, kept as the qualified name it was written with. Phase 2 does not
resolve it to a concrete enum table — `is_assignable`only needs the*kind*(enum values are assignable to`int`), and hover shows the qualified name.
- [Inner](https://docs.rs/struct.InnerClassRef.html)- Class - Ref
- A reference to an **inner**`class Name:`declared inside a script file. Identity = the declaring file (a`FileId.0`) + the dotted path to the inner class within it (`Inner`, or`Outer.Inner`when nested). The analyzer collapses the meta-vs-instance distinction (like a`class_name`/`ScriptRef`): the same`Ty::InnerClass`is the class value (`Inner.CONST`,`Inner.new()`) and an instance of it (`Inner.new().method()`).
- [Script](https://docs.rs/struct.ScriptRefId.html)- RefId
- An opaque reference to another `.gd`script (by`class_name`/path). Resolved to a concrete type only in Phase 3; in Phase 2 it never appears (the seam returns`Ty::Unknown`
- [Signal](https://docs.rs/struct.SignalSigId.html)- SigId
- An interned signal signature id (Phase 3+).
- [Typed](https://docs.rs/struct.TypedBinding.html)- Binding
- A typed binding: its `Ty`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Assign](https://docs.rs/enum.Assign.html)
- The outcome of `is_assignable`
- [Ty](https://docs.rs/enum.Ty.html)
- A Phase-2 type. `Clone`not`Copy`(the`Box`es in`Array`/`Dict`).
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.TypeSource.html)- Source
- How a binding’s type was established (Playbook §2). The ordering is load-bearing: a type is
*hard*(statically enforced) iff its source is greater than`TypeSource::Inferred`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_assignable.html)- assignable
- Whether a value of type `from`may be assigned to a slot of type`to`(the engine’s`check_type_compatibility`, ported — Playbook §3.5).**Order matters.**
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_elemref.html)- elemref
- Resolve a typed-container element `ElemRef``Ty`
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_tyref.html)- tyref
- Resolve an engine-API `TyRef``Ty`

# gdscript_hir::body - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/body/index.html

## Expand description

Body lowering (Playbook §3.1/§3.4): a function body (or a class-level initializer
expression) lowered from the CST into a flat arena of [ Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)/

[addressed by](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)

`Stmt`[/](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprId.html)

`ExprId`[, plus a](https://docs.rs/struct.StmtId.html)

`StmtId`[mapping every](https://docs.rs/struct.BodySourceMap.html)

`BodySourceMap`[back to its byte range. Every IDE feature (hover, inlay, completion) maps a cursor offset →](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprId.html)

`ExprId``ExprId` through
this source map, then reads the inferred type from [.](https://docs.rs/infer/index.html)

`crate::infer`Lowering is a pure function of the CST: no engine API, no name resolution, no types. Type
annotations (`is`/`as`/`var`/param/`for`) are kept as [ AstPtr](https://docs.rs/struct.AstPtr.html)s to their

`TypeRef` nodes
and resolved later, so this stage never depends on the model.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html)
- A lowered function body, or a single class-level initializer expression.
- [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.BodySourceMap.html)- Source - Map
- Maps every `ExprId``StmtId``ExprId`) is the tightest containing expression.
- [ExprId](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprId.html)
- An index into `Body::exprs`
- [ForLoop](https://docs.rs/struct.ForLoop.html)
- A `for var [: T] in iter:`loop.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalVar.html)- Var
- A local `var`/`const`declaration.
- [Match](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchArm.html)- Arm
- One `match`arm.
- [Match](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchBind.html)- Bind
- One `var x`capture in a`match`pattern — a local binding (so navigation can find/rename it).
- [Param](https://docs.rs/struct.ParamBinding.html)- Binding
- A function / lambda parameter binding.
- [StmtId](https://docs.rs/struct.StmtId.html)
- An index into `Body::stmts`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [BinOp](https://docs.rs/enum.BinOp.html)
- A binary operator.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)
- A lowered expression. Children are referenced by `ExprId`
- [Literal](https://docs.rs/enum.Literal.html)
- A literal’s kind (the value text lives in the CST; only the kind drives typing).
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)
- A lowered statement.
- [UnOp](https://docs.rs/enum.UnOp.html)
- A prefix unary operator.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [body](https://docs.rs/fn.body.html)
- Recover the function node for `ptr`from`root`and lower its body.
- [body_](https://docs.rs/fn.body_of_decl_stmt.html)- of_ - decl_ - stmt
- Lower a class-level `VarDecl`/`ConstDecl`node into a`Body``crate::infer`
- [body_](https://docs.rs/fn.body_of_expr.html)- of_ - expr
- Lower a single expression node into a `Body``var`/`const`initializer).
- [body_](https://docs.rs/fn.body_of_func.html)- of_ - func
- Lower a `FuncDecl`node into a`Body`

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/type.Block.html)
- A lowered block: its statements, in order.

### Missing

An unlowerable / recovered expression (typed `Error`, suppresses cascade).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Literal)

### Literal([Literal](https://docs.rs/enum.Literal.html))

A literal.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Name)

### Name([SmolStr](https://docs.rs/smol_str/0.3.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smol_str/struct.SmolStr.html))

A bare identifier reference.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SelfExpr)

### SelfExpr

`self`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Super)

### Super

`super`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Bin)

### Bin

A binary expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unary)

### Unary

A prefix unary expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ternary)

### Ternary

`a if c else b`.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Call)

### Call

`callee(args…)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Field)

### Field

`receiver.name`.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Index)

### Index

`base[index]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Is)

### Is

`operand is [not] T` — always `bool`; narrows on the true branch.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Cast)

### Cast

`operand as T` — optimistic downcast to `T`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.In)

### In

`lhs [not] in rhs` — always `bool`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Await)

### Await([ExprId](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprId.html))

`await operand`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Array)

`[a, b, …]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Dict)

`{ k: v, … }` (value is `None` only on recovery).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Lambda)

### Lambda

`func(...): …` — an anonymous function (typed `Callable`).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Preload)

### Preload

`preload(path)` — a compile-time resource reference. When `path` is a constant string
literal (the only form Godot accepts), it is captured here so inference can resolve it to
the declaring file’s `ScriptRef` (M3); a non-literal argument leaves `path` `None` (the
seam).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.GetNode)

### GetNode

`$Path` / `%Unique` / `get_node("…")` — a node-path access. In Phase 2 this was always
`Object(Node)`; Phase-4 M1 resolves the literal path against the owning scene to the node’s
concrete type. A computed `get_node(var)` keeps `path: None` (stays `Node`, never warns).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Paren)

### Paren([ExprId](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprId.html))

`(inner)`.

# gdscript_hir::infer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/infer/index.html

## Expand description

Gradual type inference (Playbook §3.3–§3.6 + §5): a single forward, bottom-up,
bidirectional walk over a lowered [ Body](https://docs.rs/body/struct.Body.html). No unification variables — types flow forward
from annotations, literals, and the engine API (rust-analyzer’s

*structure*, Pyright’s gradual

*semantics*).

The walk memoizes every expression’s [ Ty](https://docs.rs/ty/enum.Ty.html) in

[(the source of hover + inlay), does flow-scoped](https://docs.rs/struct.InferenceResult.html#structfield.expr_ty)

`InferenceResult::expr_ty``is`/`as` narrowing over the lexical guarded sub-tree, and
raises the §5 type diagnostics. The load-bearing invariant: a `Variant`/`Unknown`/`Error`
receiver is *uninformative*— it never fires

`UNSAFE_*`, never cascades — so cross-file code
(which lands on `Unknown` via the seam) produces zero false diagnostics.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Binding](https://docs.rs/struct.Binding.html)
- A typed local binding — the unit hover + inlay hints read for `var`/param/`for`names.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileInference.html)- Inference
- The full single-file inference: the item tree, every inferred unit, and the merged §5 diagnostics. The whole-file entry point the IDE layer consumes.
- [Inference](https://docs.rs/struct.InferenceResult.html)- Result
- The result of inferring one body.
- [Unit](https://docs.rs/struct.Unit.html)
- One inferred unit of a file: a function body or a class field’s initializer, with its
lowered `Body``InferenceResult`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Binding](https://docs.rs/enum.BindingKind.html)- Kind
- What kind of binding a `Binding`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [CYCLIC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CYCLIC_INHERITANCE.html)- INHERITANCE
- A genuine `extends`cycle: a file’s base chain transitively returns to itself (`A extends B`,`B extends A`). Illegal in Godot (`gdscript_analyzer.cpp`raises it). Only the`extends`inheritance chain cycles — a`preload`/`load`cycle is legal at runtime and is NOT reported.
- [INFERENCE_](https://docs.rs/constant.INFERENCE_ON_VARIANT.html)- ON_ - VARIANT
- `:=`/ inferred binding from a statically-- `Variant`value.
- [INTEGER_](https://docs.rs/constant.INTEGER_DIVISION.html)- DIVISION
- `int / int`.
- [INVALID_](https://docs.rs/constant.INVALID_NODE_PATH.html)- NODE_ - PATH
- A `$Path`/`%Unique`/`get_node("…")`whose literal path is genuinely absent in the owning scene (only raised when the script attaches to exactly one scene — never on an`..`/absolute path or a path that descends into an instanced sub-scene we don’t see).
- [NARROWING_](https://docs.rs/constant.NARROWING_CONVERSION.html)- CONVERSION
- `float`stored into an- `int`slot.
- [SHADOWED_](https://docs.rs/constant.SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER.html)- GLOBAL_ - IDENTIFIER
- A declared `class_name`that shadows another global identifier — a duplicate user`class_name`, an engine/native class, a builtin/utility, a global enum/const, or a`*`-autoload singleton. Godot’s`gdscript_analyzer.cpp`raises this (as an error) so the global namespace stays unique.
- [TYPE_](https://docs.rs/constant.TYPE_MISMATCH.html)- MISMATCH
- Incompatible hard types (our umbrella for the engine’s `push_error`).
- [UNSAFE_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNSAFE_CALL_ARGUMENT.html)- CALL_ - ARGUMENT
- An argument whose static type needs an unsafe implicit cast (`Variant`/ a downcast) into the resolved parameter type — Godot’s per-argument value-prop warning.
- [UNSAFE_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNSAFE_METHOD_ACCESS.html)- METHOD_ - ACCESS
- A method missing on a statically-known base.
- [UNSAFE_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS.html)- PROPERTY_ - ACCESS
- A property missing on a statically-known base.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_file.html)- file
- Infer an entire file: lower its item tree, then infer every function body and every
class-field initializer against a shared `ClassScope``(api, parsed file) -> result`function).
- [infer](https://docs.rs/fn.infer.html)
- Infer one function/initializer body against a class scope: walks the lowered `body::Body``Ty``InferenceResult`
- [infer_](https://docs.rs/fn.infer_func.html)- func
- Convenience: recover a function node from its `AstPtr`

---

# gdscript_hir::flow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/flow/index.html

## Expand description

Per-body control-flow narrowing (Phase-6 Workstream 2).

A pure forward dataflow over a lowered [ Body](https://docs.rs/body/struct.Body.html) (no engine API, no

`&dyn Db`, no types — types
are layered by the checker in [consulting these facts). For each reachable statement it records the](https://docs.rs/infer/index.html)

`crate::infer`[that hold](https://docs.rs/struct.FlowFacts.html)

`FlowFacts`*before*it; the checker installs those as the active narrowing environment, replacing the old lexical

`narrowing` map. It also computes
reachability — statements after a `return`/`break`/`continue` (or where every branch diverges)
are dead, feeding `UNREACHABLE_CODE` (Workstream 1 owns the emission).**Soundness over precision (the 1.0 invariant).** When unsure we *widen* (drop a fact), never
narrow wrongly: a join is an intersection, a reassignment / opaque call invalidates, a loop body
is entered with its assignments widened (no back-edge fixpoint). A wrong narrowing would hide a
real `UNSAFE_*` or assert an absent member — both worse than over-warning. The checker keeps the
load-bearing `is_uninformative` + widen-only gate when it *consumes* a fact (M1).

GDScript’s control flow is fully structured (reducible: the only non-local edges are
`break`/`continue`), so this recursive dataflow is equivalent to — and simpler + less
error-prone than — an explicit basic-block graph. It produces exactly the contract the checker
(M1) and the warning layer (M3 `UNREACHABLE_*`) consume: per-statement entry facts +
reachability.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Assigned](https://docs.rs/struct.AssignedAnalysis.html)- Analysis
- The locals **definitely**assigned a value at each statement’s entry — the intersection over all incoming control-flow paths. A typed-no-initializer local read while absent here is a read-before-assign. The sound dual of narrowing: grow-only + intersect-at-merge, and*simpler*— a callee cannot assign a caller’s function-scoped local, so there is no opaque-call / aliasing / self-rooted handling (do**not**copy those arms from the narrowing analyzer).
- [Flow](https://docs.rs/struct.FlowAnalysis.html)- Analysis
- The result of flowing a body: per-statement entry facts + the statements proven unreachable.
- [Flow](https://docs.rs/struct.FlowFacts.html)- Facts
- The narrowing facts in force at a program point (a `Place → NarrowedTy`environment).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Narrowed](https://docs.rs/enum.NarrowedTy.html)- Ty
- A narrowing fact that holds at a program point (a place narrowed to a type or proven non-null).
The type-test variants carry an `AstPtr``TypeRef`, resolved lazily by the checker against the engine model — exactly like the old`apply_narrowing`resolved its`ptr`.
- [Place](https://docs.rs/enum.Place.html)
- A narrowable place: a local/param, or a (shallow) dotted access rooted at a local or `self`. Deliberately shallow — we narrow`x`,`x.y`,`self.y`but**not**arbitrary call results (`f().y`), array indices (`a[i].y`), or anything whose identity isn’t stable under re-evaluation. Shallowness is what keeps narrowing sound under mutation/aliasing (the 1.0 cut).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [analyze](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze.html)
- Run the forward dataflow over a lowered body, producing per-statement entry facts + reachability.
- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_assigned.html)- assigned
- Run definite-assignment over `body`’s top-level statements (recursing into`if`/`for`/`while`/`match`blocks but**not**lambda bodies — those get a fresh scope and are left unchecked), seeded with the function’s`params`(always assigned).
- [condition_](https://docs.rs/fn.condition_facts.html)- facts
- The narrowing facts a condition establishes on its truthy (or falsy) edge — exposed so the
checker can apply `and`/`or`short-circuit narrowing*within*a condition expression (the RHS of`a and b`is typed under`a`’s then-facts,`a or b`’s under`a`’s else-facts).

---

# gdscript_hir::project - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/project/index.html

## Expand description

`project.godot` autoload parsing (Playbook §3.M4).

`project.godot` is a Godot `ConfigFile` (INI-like: `[section]` headers, `key=value`,
typed-Variant values). We do **not** evaluate full Variant values — the analyzer needs only
the `[autoload]` section, which is line-oriented `Name="*res://path"`. This is a deliberate
minimal scan (not a `VariantParser` port): track the current `[section]`, and within
`[autoload]` split each line on the first `=`, take the bare LHS as the autoload name and the
dequoted RHS as the resource path. The leading `*` on the path is the **singleton/global**
flag (`project_settings.cpp`: `begins_with("*")` → `is_singleton`, then `substr(1)` strips it);
a non-`*` autoload is loaded at `/root/Name` but is **not** a global identifier.

Pure (`fn(&str) -> Vec<AutoloadEntry>`) and wasm-clean — the host injects the text.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Autoload](https://docs.rs/struct.AutoloadEntry.html)- Entry
- One `[autoload]`entry from`project.godot`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_autoloads.html)- autoloads
- Parse the `[autoload]`entries from`project.godot`text. Robust to comments, blank lines, and other sections; never panics on malformed input (a bad line is skipped).
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_engine_version.html)- engine_ - version
- Parse the Godot engine `(major, minor)`version from`project.godot`’s`[application]``config/features=PackedStringArray("4.3", "Forward Plus", …)`line. Godot writes the engine version as the first`<major>.<minor>`entry of that array; the rest are rendering/feature tags. Returns the first version-shaped entry, or`None`if the line is absent or carries none. A deliberate minimal scan (not a`VariantParser`port); robust to malformed input (never panics).
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_warning_settings.html)- warning_ - settings
- Parse the `debug/gdscript/warnings/*`settings from`project.godot`into a`WarningSettings``engine`. Keys live under`[debug]`as`gdscript/warnings/<tail>`(Godot groups a setting by its first path segment).`<tail>`is`enable`/`treat_warnings_as_errors`/`exclude_addons`(bools) or a code’s lowercased setting-name mapped to a`0|1|2`(Ignore/Warn/Error) level. A deliberate minimal scan (not a`VariantParser`port); robust to malformed input (a bad line is skipped).`directory_rules`(Godot master, a typed-Variant dict) is not parsed — see`TECH_DEBT.md`.

---

# gdscript_hir::queries - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-hir/0.5.3/gdscript_hir/queries/index.html

## Expand description

The salsa-tracked entry points for the semantic layer, layered on `gdscript-db`’s
[ parse](https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_db/fn.parse.html) query.

These are the memoized queries the IDE layer drives. The heavy lifting stays in
[ crate::item_tree](https://docs.rs/item_tree/index.html) /

[as plain](https://docs.rs/infer/index.html)

`crate::infer``(parsed file) -> value` functions; this
module only wraps them so their results are cached per revision and recomputed
incrementally. [is the](https://docs.rs/fn.item_tree.html)

`item_tree`**firewall**query (Playbook §4): it reads only the parse, never a function body, so an unchanged set of signatures backdates across body edits.

Phase-3 note: cross-file resolution (the `resolve_external` seam) is still `Ty::Unknown`
here — M1 threads `&dyn Db` + `FileId` into inference to light it up. M0 only swaps the
cache engine; the single-file results are byte-identical.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Autoload](https://docs.rs/struct.AutoloadRegistry.html)- Registry
- The project’s autoload **singletons**(`*`-flagged`[autoload]`entries) — the bare names that resolve as globals in code. Maps each singleton name → its resource path (M4). Non-singleton autoloads are deliberately excluded (loaded-but-not-global). Keyed on`ProjectConfig``.gd`keystroke.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalRegistry.html)- Registry
- The project-wide global `class_name`registry: each registered name → the file declaring it.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneAttach.html)- Attach
- Where a script (`.gd`) is attached in a scene: the owning scene file + the node carrying the`script = ExtResource(...)`.`$Path`in that script resolves relative to this node.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneContext.html)- Context
- The resolved owning-scene context for a script — the scene file, its model, the attach node, and
whether the attachment is ambiguous (multi-scene). Returned by `scene_context`
- [Script](https://docs.rs/struct.ScriptClass.html)- Class
- A script class’s own members, by name, plus its resolved `extends`base — the**offset-free projection**a cross-file reference resolves against. Reads only`item_tree`signatures (+ annotation/base resolution), never bodies or byte ranges, so it backdates on body edits (the cross-file firewall). Member lookup walks the base chain (M2): own members here, inherited ones via`base`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Member](https://docs.rs/enum.MemberSig.html)- Sig
- One member of a script class, as a cross-file reference sees it (a resolved type, never a byte range).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_file.html)- file
- Whole-file inference for `file`. With no engine model available (`wasm32`, until the host wires the fetched blob in) this is an empty result — matching the Phase-2 graceful path.
- [autoload_](https://docs.rs/fn.autoload_registry.html)- registry
- The project-wide autoload-singleton registry, parsed from `project.godot`(M4). Only`*`-flagged entries become globals; a duplicate name keeps the first (deterministic).
- [class_](https://docs.rs/fn.class_name_collisions.html)- name_ - collisions
- The set of global `class_name`s declared by**more than one**file in`root`— the shadowing diagnostic’s cross-file half. Mirrors`global_registry``file_class_name``global_registry`keeps the*first*declarer silently; this query names the duplicates so`crate::infer::analyze_file`
- [engine_](https://docs.rs/fn.engine_version.html)- version
- The Godot engine `(major, minor)`declared by`project.godot`’s`[application]``config/features`, or`None`if unspecified. Keyed on`ProjectConfig``.gd`body edits — the same cross-file firewall as`autoload_registry`
- [file_](https://docs.rs/fn.file_class_name.html)- class_ - name
- A file’s `class_name`, if it declares one — the**offset-free projection**of its item tree that`global_registry``item_tree(file).class_name`(never a byte range), so a body edit re-runs`item_tree`but this query*backdates*(its value is unchanged), leaving the registry — and everything cross-file — undisturbed by a keystroke.
- [global_](https://docs.rs/fn.global_registry.html)- registry
- The project-wide global `class_name`registry. Keyed on the`SourceRoot``file_class_name``class_name`keeps the first by`FileId`order (the file set is sorted), so resolution is deterministic. Collision*diagnostics*(warning at each duplicate declaration) are the separate`class_name_collisions`
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_scene_path.html)- scene_ - path
- Whether a `res://`path is a*text*scene/resource we parse (`.tscn`/`.tres`). Binary`.scn`/`.res`are detected-and-degraded by the parser, but we don’t waste a parse on a`.gd`.
- [item_](https://docs.rs/fn.item_tree.html)- tree
- The item tree for `file`(signatures only — the body-edit firewall). Memoized; recomputes when the parse changes but backdates when the resulting signatures are unchanged.
- [project_](https://docs.rs/fn.project_engine_version.html)- engine_ - version
- Convenience over `engine_version``(major, minor)`, or`None`when there is no`project.godot`or it declares no version.
- [res_](https://docs.rs/fn.res_path_registry.html)- path_ - registry
- The project-wide `res:// path → FileId`registry (M3): the map`preload("res://x.gd")`and`extends "res://x.gd"`resolve through. Keyed on the`SourceRoot``res_path`salsa-input field.`res_path`is a*separate*input field from`text`(salsa tracks input fields individually), so this registry**backdates across body edits**exactly like`global_registry``FileId`order (the file set is sorted), matching`global_registry`’s policy.
- [scene_](https://docs.rs/fn.scene_context.html)- context
- The owning-scene context for the script in `file`(M1): the scene’s`FileId``$Path`/`%Unique`/`get_node("…")`can resolve (and go-to-def can jump into the`.tscn`).`None`when the project has no scene attaching this script (the overwhelmingly common single-file / dynamic-UI case → node paths stay`Node`).
- [scene_](https://docs.rs/fn.scene_model.html)- model
- The parsed `SceneModel``file`(M1) — memoized; recomputes only when the file text changes. A non-scene file (a`.gd`, or no`res://`path) yields an empty model (so the query is total). The pure`gdscript_scene::parse_scene`is the cache body; this just wraps + gates it.
- [script_](https://docs.rs/fn.script_class.html)- class
- The member table of the script in `file`. Member types are resolved against the engine model and the registry (a member typed as another`class_name`resolves to its`ScriptRef`).
- [script_](https://docs.rs/fn.script_ref_name.html)- ref_ - name
- The `class_name`behind a`ScriptRef``Ty::label`cannot resolve this on its own — it has only the engine model, not the project registry.
- [script_](https://docs.rs/fn.script_scene_attachments.html)- scene_ - attachments
- **Every**scene that attaches the script at- `res_path`—- `(scene file, attach node)`pairs in scan order. Single-scene scripts have one entry; the rare multi-scene script has several (the basis for- `$Path`- **union typing**, M2 §6.3 — type a path as the common base across all scenes). Same firewall as- `script_scene_index`- `.gd`edits).
- [script_](https://docs.rs/fn.script_scene_index.html)- scene_ - index
- The project-wide **script → owning scene**index (M1): each`.gd`’s`res://`path → the (first) scene + node that attaches it. Built by scanning every scene’s`ext_resources`for a`type="Script"`reference. Keyed on the`SourceRoot``scene_model``.gd`**body**edit never touches a`.tscn`text, so this**backdates across**— the firewall (a scene edit correctly invalidates it). A duplicate (one script in many scenes) keeps the first by`.gd`keystrokes`FileId`order (the slice’s single-scene policy).
- [suppression_](https://docs.rs/fn.suppression_map.html)- map
- The per-file `@warning_ignore[_start|_restore]`suppression map (Workstream 1). Keyed on the file’s parse — CST byte ranges are stable across incremental edits — so it recomputes only when the file text changes, never on a warning-setting edit.
- [warning_](https://docs.rs/fn.warning_settings.html)- settings
- The project’s resolved warning settings, parsed from `project.godot`’s`debug/gdscript/warnings/*`(Workstream 1). Keyed on`ProjectConfig``.gd`body, so**editing a warning level invalidates only this query + the downstream gate, never**— the salsa-cacheability invariant the gating seam depends on (W1 §3.4/§6).`analyze_file`/`item_tree`/`infer`
